lessons.desc: An Eulerian path visits every edge exactly once (Eulerian circuit if it starts and ends at the same vertex). Hierholzer's algorithm builds it by following unused edges and splicing cycles back in. Classic problem: Reconstruct Itinerary (visit every flight edge).
lessons.q: What is the difference between an Eulerian path and a Hamiltonian path?
lessons.qsub: State the degree condition for an Eulerian circuit. · Why does Reconstruct Itinerary require lexicographic adjacency? · How do you handle the starting vertex? · What makes Eulerian easy but Hamiltonian hard?
lessons.what:
Ab tak har traversal ka goal tha: har node ek baar dekhna. Yahan goal ulta hai: har edge theek ek baar use karna — node dobara aa jaaye to chalega.

Isko Euler path kehte hain. Wapas wahin khatam ho jahan se shuru hua? To Euler circuit. Classic misaal: postman jise har gali se ek baar guzarna hai.

Ek pyaari baat: chalane se pehle hi pata chal jaata hai ki possible hai ya nahi — sirf degrees gin ke. Saare even → circuit. Theek 2 odd → path. Aur kuch → kuch nahi banta.

Hierholzer ise banata hai, aur uska tareeka thoda ajeeb hai: unused edges pe aage badhte jao. Fas gaye? Us node ko list mein daalo aur peeche hato. Aakhir mein poori list ulti karo — wahi jawab hai.
lessons.analogy:
Courier wale ko shehar ki har gali se ek baar guzarna hai — chowk pe dobara aana chalega, par gali dobara nahi.
Wo jitni door tak ja sakta hai jaata hai. Jahan aage koi nayi gali nahi bachi, wahan ruk kar wo jagah note karta hai aur peeche laut'ta hai — dekhta hai kahin beech mein koi gali chhoot to nahi gayi.
lessons.why:
Pehla test: Euler aur Hamilton ka farak. Euler = har edge ek baar, aur ye O(E) mein hal ho jaata hai. Hamilton = har node ek baar, aur wo NP-hard hai — koi tez algorithm hai hi nahi. Ek akshar ka farak, aur duniya alag.

Doosra: Reconstruct Itinerary mein log naive DFS + backtracking likhte hain aur TLE khaate hain. Hierholzer O(E) mein karta hai — kyunki wo kabhi backtrack nahi karta, bas result ulta banata hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Pehle degrees gino. Saare even → kahin se bhi shuru karo (circuit). Theek 2 odd → kisi ek odd node se shuru karo (path). Warna → possible hi nahi.
2. Ek stack lo, usme start node daalo.
3. Stack ke top node ke paas koi unused edge bachi hai? Ek uthao, wo edge hata do, aur doosre sire ko stack pe push karo.
4. Koi edge nahi bachi? Top node ko result mein daalo aur stack se pop karo.
5. Stack khaali hone tak dohrao.
6. Result ko reverse karo. Wahi Euler path hai.
7. Lexicographically chhota chahiye (Reconstruct Itinerary)? Har node ki adjacency list pehle sort kar lo.

qa.q: What is the difference between an Eulerian path and a Hamiltonian path?
qa.a: Eulerian visits every EDGE once (easy to check via degrees, O(E)). Hamiltonian visits every VERTEX once — that is NP-hard to even decide. Interviewers test that you know which is which.

qa.q: Why does Hierholzer build the answer in reverse?
qa.a: A naive DFS dead-ends when it returns to the start too early, missing side cycles. By only popping when no edges remain, cycles are deferred to the unwind phase; reversing the pops joins them into one valid path.

lessons.name: Trie Structure
lessons.desc: A tree where each node holds children keyed by character, and a flag marking word ends. Inserting/querying a word of length m costs O(m) regardless of how many words are stored — no re-scanning shared prefixes.
lessons.q: Why is a Trie faster than a Set for prefix queries?
lessons.qsub: How do you delete a word from a Trie? · What's the worst-case memory of a Trie over a hash set? · How would you auto-complete to the top-k suggestions?
lessons.what:
Google search bar mein ind type karo — turant "india", "indian railway" aa jaate hain. Poori dictionary scan kiye bina.

Agar words ek array mein hote to har naye akshar pe poora array dobara chhaanna padta. Trie ise tree bana deta hai: root se neeche har edge ek character hai, aur kisi node tak pahunchna matlab "yahan tak ka hissa ek valid prefix hai".

Har node pe ek chhota flag — isEnd — jo batata hai "yahan koi poora word khatam hota hai ya nahi". Ye flag hi "apple" aur "app" ka farak rakhta hai.

Aur asli faayda: word dhoondhne ka time sirf uski apni lambai pe depend karta hai — O(m). Dictionary mein 10 words hon ya 10 lakh, farak nahi padta.
lessons.analogy:
Phone ke contacts. R dabao — sirf R waale naam. a aur dabao — sirf "Ra" waale. Har akshar ek chhanni hai jo aage ka raasta patla karta jaata hai.
Aur "Ra" tak pahunch jaana matlab ye nahi ki "Ra" naam ka koi contact hai — wahi isEnd wali baat hai.
lessons.why:
Hash map exact match deta hai. Prefix nahi. "app se shuru hone waale saare words" — hash map ke paas iska koi jawab nahi, poora scan karna padega.

Interviewer ye dekhta hai ki tum space aur time ka tradeoff samajhte ho: thodi extra memory de kar tumne O(m) lookup guarantee kar liya, aur wo dictionary ke size n se bilkul azaad hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Root ek khaali node hai — wo kisi character ko represent nahi karta.
2. Har node ke paas children hota hai — ya to 26 ka array, ya ek Map.
3. Insert: root se shuru, word ke har character pe child dekho. Nahi hai? Bana do. Hai? Uspe utar jao.
4. Aakhri character waale node pe isEnd = true. Ye step bhoolna sabse aam bug hai.
5. Common prefix apne aap share ho jaata hai — "cat" aur "car" ka c-a hissa ek hi raasta hai.
6. Memory: worst case har word apna alag raasta — O(total characters × 26). Prefix jitne zyada share hon, utni bachat.

qa.q: Why is a Trie faster than a Set for prefix queries?
qa.a: A Set can answer 'is this word present?' in O(1) but 'which words start with this prefix?' requires scanning everything. A Trie answers startsWith in O(m) by walking the prefix — the shared structure IS the index.

qa.q: Trie vs hash map for a dictionary of words?
qa.a: Trie: O(m) prefix search, memory shared across words with common prefixes, natural for wildcards-with-DFS and prefix counting. HashMap: simpler, O(m) exact lookups, but no prefix semantics and more memory per word. For pure existence checks, the map wins; for prefix work, the trie wins.

lessons.name: Trie Insert / Search / Prefix
lessons.desc: The three operations that define a trie — insert, search, and prefix search — plus the DFS extension for wildcards and word-collection. Master the walk helper and everything else is thin.
lessons.q: How does the wildcard '.' work?
lessons.qsub: How do you count how many words start with a prefix? · What does the DFS base case return for wildcard matching? · How would you find the longest word where every prefix is also a word?
lessons.what:
Trie bana hua hai. Ab teen kaam karne hain, aur teeno mein raasta bilkul same hai — root se ek-ek character neeche utarna. Farak sirf aakhir mein hai.

Insert: missing node mile to bana do, aur aakhir mein isEnd = true.
Search: raasta hona chahiye aur isEnd bhi.
startsWith: sirf raasta hona chahiye — isEnd se koi matlab nahi.

Isiliye ek walk helper likh lo jo raasta chal ke node ya null laut'ta hai. Uske baad search aur startsWith dono ek-ek line ke ho jaate hain.

Iske aage ek DFS extension hai — wildcard . (koi bhi character) aur "is node se aage ke saare words nikaalo" — jo autocomplete banata hai.
lessons.analogy: Building jisme har manzil ek akshar hai. Insert = chadhte hue jahan manzil nahi hai wahan bana do. Search = poora raasta bana hua hai aur upar ghar bhi hai. startsWith = bas itna dekho ki utni manzil tak seedhi bani hai — upar ghar ho ya na ho.
lessons.why:
Log search aur startsWith ko ek hi samajh lete hain, ya isEnd ka check galat jagah laga dete hain. Ye ek line ka farak hi asli test hai.

Aur wildcard DFS se pata chalta hai ki tum trie ke upar recursion aur backtracking dono jod sakte ho — wahi skill Word Search II jaise hard problems mein chahiye hoti hai, jahan trie board ki backtracking ko kaat deta hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Walk helper: root se shuru, har character pe child dekho. Missing mila → null. Poora chal gaya → wo node laut'ao.
2. search(word): walk(word) se node lo. null nahi hai aur isEnd hai → true.
3. startsWith(p): walk(p) !== null. Bas.
4. Wildcard .: normal character pe seedha utar jao. . aaya to har bachche mein DFS karo — ek bhi true de de to true.
5. Collect all: node se DFS karke neeche jao, raaste ke characters jodte jao, aur jahan isEnd mile wahan word list mein daal do — par rukо mat, aage aur lambe words ho sakte hain.
6. Wildcard ka worst case O(26^dots) hai — ye caveat bolna chahiye.
where: O(m) avg, O(26^w) worst · space: O(depth)
Collect all words from a node

qa.q: How does the wildcard '.' work?
qa.a: At the wildcard position, branch into EVERY child — if any branch completes the word, it matches. That's a DFS over the fan-out, worst case exploring all children at each '.' (O(26^k) for k wildcards), but average case is fine because each level is bounded.

qa.q: Why is a Trie ideal for Word Search II?
qa.a: Backtracking over the board would rescan shared prefixes for every word. The trie lets one DFS pass carry all word matches simultaneously — the current prefix node tells you which words are still possible, pruning the board search to only live prefixes.

lessons.name: XOR Tricks
lessons.desc: XOR is its own inverse: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x. That makes it the perfect tool for cancelling duplicates — every element that appears twice vanishes, leaving only the singleton. O(n) time, O(1) space.
lessons.q: Why does XORing all elements find the singleton?
lessons.qsub: What if TWO elements appear once (find both)? · Can XOR solve the 'appears 3 times' variant? · Why is XOR O(1) space where a hash set is O(n)?
lessons.what:
Array mein har number do baar aaya hai, sirf ek akela hai. Use dhoondhna hai — O(n) time aur O(1) space mein. Hash map allowed nahi.

XOR ke do niyam yahan sab kuch kar dete hain: x ^ x = 0 (khud se XOR karo, gayab) aur x ^ 0 = x (0 se XOR karo, wahi ka wahi).

Matlab: poore array ko ek saath XOR kar do. Jo jodi mein hain wo ek doosre ko kaat denge, aur jo akela hai wahi bachega. Order se koi farak nahi — jodi kahin bhi ho, cancel ho jaati hai.

Shart: baaki sab even baar aane chahiye. Teen baar aane waale pe ye cancellation kaam nahi karega — wahan bilkul alag trick chahiye.
lessons.analogy:
Khaate mein har udhaar ke saamne uski wapsi bhi likhi hai. Do baar likhi hui har entry apne aap kat jaati hai. Aakhir mein sirf wahi entry bachti hai jiska koi jodidaar nahi tha.
Aur ye kis order mein kaate, isse koi farak nahi padta — jodi to jodi hai.
lessons.why:
Ye seedha ek O(n) space wale hash map solution ko O(1) space bana deta hai. Interviewer isi jump ko dekhta hai.

Aur follow-up hamesha aata hai: "agar do numbers akele hon to?" Jawab: sab XOR karo — jo mila wo un dono ka XOR hai. Uska koi bhi set bit uthao — us bit pe dono numbers alag hain. Us bit se array ko do group mein baanto, aur har group ka XOR alag nikaalo. Ye samjha ke bol dena bada point hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. result = 0 se shuru karo.
2. Har element ko result ke saath XOR karte jao.
3. Jo bhi even baar aaya hai wo apne aap kat gaya — x ^ x = 0.
4. Jo odd baar aaya wo bacha reh gaya — 0 ^ x = x.
5. Missing number: 0..n ke saare index aur saari values ek saath XOR karo. Har maujood number apne index se kat jaayega, aur missing bach jaayega.
6. Do singletons: sab XOR karo → a ^ b mila. diff = xor & -xor se koi ek alag bit uthao, us bit ke hisaab se do group banao, dono ka XOR alag — wahi a aur b hain.

qa.q: Why does XORing all elements find the singleton?
qa.a: XOR is commutative and associative, and x ^ x = 0. Every duplicate pair cancels to 0, and 0 ^ singleton = singleton. Everything left after full cancellation is the number that appears once.

qa.q: How does XOR find a missing number?
qa.a: XOR the array with every index plus n. The value at each present index appears twice (once from the array, once from the index loop) and cancels. Only the missing number's index appears once — that's the answer.

lessons.name: Bit Shifts & Masks
lessons.desc: Left shift << multiplies by 2, right shift >> divides by 2. Combined with bitwise AND/OR and masks (1 << k), you can read, set, clear, and toggle individual bits — the basis of bitmask DP and packed-state problems.
lessons.q: How do you check if a number is a power of two in one expression?
lessons.qsub: How do you iterate every subset of a set of n elements? · What does >>> vs >> do with negative numbers? · How do you reverse the bits of a 32-bit integer?
lessons.what:
Ek user ke liye 5 permissions rakhni hain — read, write, execute, share, delete. 5 alag boolean banana fizool lagta hai. Ek hi number ke andar 5 bits mein poori state fit ho jaati hai.

Left shift x << k — bits k jagah baayein, yaani × 2^k. Right shift x >> k — ulta, ÷ 2^k.

Mask = (1 << k) — ek aisa number jisme sirf k-va bit 1 hai, baaki sab 0. Isi ek cheez se tum kisi bhi bit ko padh, set, clear ya toggle kar sakte ho — baaki bits ko chhue bina.

Yahi neev hai bitmask DP aur subset enumeration ki — jahan poori state ek integer mein pack ho jaati hai.
lessons.analogy: Switchboard pe 8 switch, har ek alag appliance ka. Ek switch on/off karne ke liye poora board hilana nahi padta — sirf usi ek ko chhoote ho. Mask wahi "sirf ye ek switch" batane ka tarika hai.
lessons.why:
Ye subset enumeration aur bitmask DP ki neev hai — Phase 7 aur 8 mein baar-baar chahiye hogi.

Aur do JS-specific trap hain jo interviewer khaas dekhta hai. Pehla: operator precedence — x & 1 << k !== 0 galat parse hota hai, brackets zaroori hain. Doosra: >> sign rakhta hai, >>> nahi — negative numbers pe ye farak sab bigaad deta hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Padho: (x >> k) & 1 — bit ko neeche laao aur 1 se AND. Ya (x & (1 << k)) !== 0.
2. Set: x | (1 << k) — OR sirf us bit ko 1 karta hai, baaki waise hi.
3. Clear: x & ~(1 << k) — mask ka ulta lo, usme sirf wahi bit 0 hai — AND se wahi girta hai.
4. Toggle: x ^ (1 << k) — XOR palat deta hai.
5. Subsets: n cheezon ke saare subsets = 0 se 2^n - 1 tak ke numbers. Har number ek subset hai — jis bit pe 1 hai, wo cheez shaamil hai.
6. JS mein bitwise ops 32-bit pe chalte hain. 1 << 31 negative ho jaata hai, aur 1 << 32 wapas 1 — shift wrap ho jaata hai.

qa.q: How do you check if a number is a power of two in one expression?
qa.a: n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) === 0. n - 1 flips the lowest set bit and all zeros below it; if n was a pure power of two, n & (n-1) clears its only set bit → 0. Any other n keeps at least one bit → nonzero.

qa.q: What is a bitmask and when is it worth it?
qa.a: A single integer whose bits encode a set of choices — e.g. bit k = 1 means element k is used. It turns subset/state operations into O(1) integer ops, the backbone of bitmask DP (Traveling Salesman). It's worth it when n ≤ 20 and states are combinations.

lessons.name: n & (n-1) Trick
lessons.desc: The expression n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit of n. Repeating it counts set bits in O(number of set bits) — faster than scanning every bit — and it powers 'is this a power of two?'
lessons.q: Why is this faster than shifting every bit?
lessons.qsub: How many iterations does the loop run for a number with k set bits? · How does this relate to the power-of-two check? · What happens when n = 0 in the counting loop?
lessons.what:
Number ke binary mein kitne 1 hain, ye ginna hai. Naive tarika: 32 bits ek-ek karke check karo — chahe sirf 2 hi set bits hon, loop poore 32 baar chalta hai.

n & (n - 1) ek shortcut hai: ye hamesha sabse neeche waala set bit gira deta hai, aur baaki sab bits ko chhoota bhi nahi.

Kaise: n - 1 karne se sabse neeche waala 1 gir'ta hai aur uske aage ke saare 0 palat kar 1 ban jaate hain (borrow). Ab n ke saath AND karo — wo palte hue bits wapas 0 ho jaate hain (original mein wahan 0 hi tha), aur upar ke bits waise hi rehte hain.

Isliye loop utni hi baar chalega jitne set bits the — 32 baar nahi. Aur ek muft ka bonus: n & (n-1) === 0 matlab sirf ek set bit tha, yaani power of two.
lessons.analogy:
Building ki saari lights on hain aur ginni hain. Ek jaadui switch hai jo har dabane pe sirf sabse neeche wali on light bujha deta hai, baaki sab waise ke waise.
Jitni baar switch dabana pada, utni hi lights on thi. Bas.
lessons.why:
Hamming weight O(32) se O(set bits) ban jaata hai. Par asli baat ye hai ki interviewer "kyun kaam karta hai" poochta hai — aur wahan borrow waali wajah bolni padti hai, formula nahi.

Aur ek chachera bhai hai jo confuse karta hai: n & -n. Wo ulta kaam karta hai — sirf sabse neeche waala bit rakhta hai, baaki sab hata deta hai. Do bilkul alag cheezein hain.

Kaise sochein:

1. n - 1 lo: sabse neeche waala 1 0 ban jaata hai, aur uske daayein ke saare 0 1 ban jaate hain.
2. n & (n - 1): wo palte hue bits AND se wapas 0 (original mein wahan 0 tha).
3. Upar ke bits dono mein same the — wo bilkul nahi badle.
4. Natija: theek ek set bit gaya, baaki sab safe.
5. Count: while (n) { n &= n - 1; count++ } — har chakkar ek set bit khaata hai.
6. Power of two: n > 0 && (n & (n-1)) === 0 — ek hi set bit tha, isliye ek baar mein 0. n > 0 ka check zaroori hai.

qa.q: Why is this faster than shifting every bit?
qa.a: Shifting checks all 32 bits regardless. n & (n-1) skips every 0 bit entirely — the loop runs once per SET bit. For sparse numbers like 8 (1000), that's 1 iteration instead of 32.

qa.q: What does n & -n compute?
qa.a: The value of the lowest set bit as a power of two. -n is two's complement (invert + 1), which keeps the lowest 1 bit and flips everything above — ANDing with n isolates exactly that bit. Useful for Fenwick trees and lowest-bit manipulation.

lessons.name: Memoization vs Tabulation
lessons.desc: Two ways to compute the same DP table. Memoization (top-down): recursive with a cache, compute only needed states. Tabulation (bottom-up): iterative, fill a table in dependency order. Same result, different trade-offs.
lessons.q: When should you prefer memoization over tabulation?
lessons.qsub: Why does naive Fibonacci blow up to O(2^n)? · What is a 'state' in DP terms? · When can you roll the table into variables?
lessons.what:
fib(40) recursively chalao — minute lag jaate hain. Kyunki fib(35) jaisi subproblem hazaaron baar dobara compute hoti hai.

Do ilaaj hain, dono wahi wastage rokte hain — bas direction alag hai.

Memoization (top-down): wahi recursion rakho jo tumne socha tha, bas ek cache jod do. Pehli baar answer nikaal ke store karo, dobara wahi call aaye to seedha cache se.

Tabulation (bottom-up): recursion hata do. Base case se shuru karke ek table aage bharte jao, jab tak final answer na aa jaaye.

Table dono mein wahi banti hai. Interview mein hamesha memo se shuru karo — kyunki wo tumhari recursion mein sirf ek line ka change hai.
lessons.analogy:
Exam ki practice. Memo = jab bhi koi naya sawaal solve karo, jawab notebook mein likh lo — wahi sawaal dobara aaye to seedha dekh lo.
Tabulation = pehle hi saare aasaan sawaalon ke jawab bana ke rakh do, phir unse mushkil waale banate jao — kabhi peeche jaane ki zaroorat hi nahi.
lessons.why:
Interviewer dono ka tradeoff poochta hai. Memo likhna aasaan hai — recursion se seedha nikal aata hai — par call stack ki wajah se bade input pe overflow ho sakta hai, aur wo sirf zaroori states compute karta hai.

Tabulation thodi planning maangta hai (dependency order sahi hona chahiye), par usually tez aur safe hai, aur usi se space optimization possible hoti hai — "sirf pichhli do value chahiye? To poora array mat rakho."

Aur ek sawaal lagbhag hamesha aata hai: "isko bottom-up mein convert kar sakte ho?"

Kaise sochein:

1. Pehle brute-force recursion likho. Sahi hone do, tez baad mein karenge.
2. State pehchano — call ke beech jo parameters badalte hain, wahi state hai.
3. Ek memo (array ya Map) daalo, key = state. Function ke shuru mein cache check, aakhir mein cache mein likho.
4. Bottom-up mein badalna ho: table ka size = states ki ginti, loop ka order dependency ke hisaab se — jo pehle chahiye wo pehle bharo.
5. Base cases table mein seed kar do.
6. Aakhir mein dekho: har dp[i] sirf pichhle 1-2 pe depend karta hai? To array hata ke variables rakh lo — O(1) space.
where: O(#states × cost per state) · space: O(#states) + O(depth)
O(#states × cost per state) · space: O(table) or optimized O(1)-O(n)

qa.q: When should you prefer memoization over tabulation?
qa.a: Memoization is easier to write correctly (just add a cache to working recursion), only computes reachable states, and reads naturally. Prefer it unless recursion depth is a risk or the interviewer wants the iterative version — then write tabulation.

qa.q: What's the key to a space-optimized DP?
qa.a: Figure out the dependency window — if dp[i] only needs dp[i-1] and dp[i-2], keep two variables instead of the full table. 2D problems often reduce to two rolling rows (or one) when each cell only reads the row above.

lessons.name: Identifying DP
lessons.desc: The pattern-recognition step: a problem is DP when it has overlapping subproblems (same sub-solve computed many times) and optimal substructure (best answer built from best sub-answers). 'Count ways', 'min/max cost', and 'is it possible' phrasing are strong signals.
lessons.q: How do you recognize DP vs a greedy solution?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between 'count ways' and 'min cost' recurrences? · Why does a single counterexample kill a greedy approach? · How do you define a state for a 2-string problem like Edit Distance?
lessons.what:
Naya problem saamne hai. Pehla faisla: greedy, plain recursion, ya DP? Ye galat chunna sabse aam galti hai.

Do cheezein check karo. Overlapping subproblems — brute-force recursion ka tree kheencho, aur dekho ki wahi exact subproblem (same parameters) baar-baar dikh raha hai kya.

Optimal substructure — poore ka best jawab, chhote hisson ke best jawaabon se seedha ban jaata hai kya, bina kisi purane faisle ko dobara sochne ke.

Dono mile → DP. Sirf ek mila → plain recursion ya greedy. Aur ek shortcut: problem ka phrase hi aksar bata deta hai — "kitne tarike", "kam se kam cost", "ho sakta hai kya".
lessons.analogy:
Seedhi chadh rahe ho, har step pe soch rahe ho "1 loon ya 2". Thodi der mein dikhta hai ki "step 5 se aage kya" wala wahi sawaal alag-alag raaston se baar-baar aa raha hai.
Jab ek hi sawaal baar-baar poochna pade — wahi overlapping subproblem hai, aur wahi cache lagane ka signal hai.
lessons.why:
Ye step interview mein seedha nahi poocha jaata — par judge hota hai. Agar tum state define kiye bina seedha code likhna shuru kar do, interviewer turant samajh jaata hai ki DP samajh nahi aayi.

Aur greedy ka trap yaad rakho: greedy ek counterexample se mar jaata hai. Coin Change mein [1, 3, 4] se amount 6 banao — greedy 4+1+1 = 3 coins deta hai, par sahi jawab 3+3 = 2 hai. Saabit nahi kar paa rahe? To DP maano.

Kaise sochein:

1. Brute-force recursion socho aur uska call tree kheencho (chhote input pe).
2. Wahi subproblem dobara dikha? → overlapping. Cache kaam aayega.
3. State define karo: "ek call se doosri call mein kya-kya badal raha hai?" Ek index → dp[i]. Do index → dp[i][j]. Index + bacha hua budget → dp[i][w].
4. Recurrence pehle shabdon mein likho, code mein nahi: "is jagah ka best = ye choice ya wo choice, jo behtar ho".
5. Operator phrase se chuno: "kitne tarike" → +. "kam/zyada se zyada" → min/max. "ho sakta hai" → ||.
6. Base case likho — sabse chhota input jiska jawab seedha pata ho.

qa.q: How do you recognize DP vs a greedy solution?
qa.a: Try greedy: does the locally best choice always lead to the global best? If you can't prove it and counterexamples exist, it's DP. Tell-tale: 'subsets/subsets with constraint' where the answer depends on ALL previous choices, not just the last one.

qa.q: What's the first question to design any DP?
qa.a: 'What is the state?' — the tuple of everything that changes between recursive calls. For Climbing Stairs it's i (steps remaining). For Knapsack it's (index, remaining capacity). Get the state right and the recurrence usually writes itself.

lessons.name: 1D DP
lessons.desc: dp[i] depends only on earlier indices (usually i-1, i-2). The Fibonacci, House Robber, and Decode Ways family. The simplest DP class — master it before anything 2D.
lessons.q: How do you choose the recurrence for a 1D DP?
lessons.qsub: When does dp[i] depend on i-2 vs all previous indices? · How do you optimize LIS from O(n²) to O(n log n)? · What's the base case trap in Decode Ways ('0' handling)?
lessons.what:
Seedhi chadh rahe ho, ek baar mein 1 ya 2 step. n-va step tak kitne tarike hain? Yahan jawab sirf pichhle ek-do steps pe depend karta hai — koi purani history nahi chahiye.

Isi shakal ko 1D DP kehte hain: ek array dp jahan dp[i] position i tak ka jawab rakhta hai, aur wo dp[i-1] ya dp[i-2] se banta hai.

Fibonacci, House Robber, Decode Ways — teeno isi parivaar mein hain. Sirf transition rule alag hai: kahin jodna hai, kahin max lena hai.

Aur ek muft ka faayda: agar sirf pichhli do value chahiye, to poora array rakhne ki zaroorat hi nahi — do variable kaafi hain. O(n) space se O(1).
lessons.analogy:
Ek chor mohalle ki planning kar raha hai — do bagal-bagal ke ghar ek saath nahi lut sakte. Har ghar pe uska faisla sirf ek baat pe tika hai: "pichhle ek-do ghar tak ka best kya tha?"
Poore mohalle ka itihaas dobara sochne ki zaroorat hi nahi padti.
lessons.why:
Ye pehla DP pattern hai jo interview mein aata hai, aur ye state definition ka sabse saaf version sikhata hai — ek index pe ek value.

Agar yahan confusion hai (dp[i] ka matlab kya hai, kaunse pichhle states chahiye), to 2D aur bitmask DP mein aur zyada confusion hogi.

Aur base case ka trap yahin hai: Decode Ways mein '0' ka handling, House Robber mein n = 0 aur n = 1 — yahin sabse zyada log fisalte hain.

Kaise sochein:

1. dp[i] ka matlab ek line mein likho — "pehle i elements tak ka best/count".
2. Base case: i = 0 aur i = 1 alag se sochо. Khaali input aur ek element — ye do case pehle likh do.
3. Recurrence shabdon mein: "is element ko lo, ya chhodo — jo behtar ho".
4. House Robber: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]). Chhodo → dp[i-1]. Lo → pichhla chhodna padega, isliye dp[i-2].
5. Poora array bharo, dp[n-1] hi jawab hai.
6. Space: sirf pichhli do value chahiye? Do variable rakh lo — par order dhyaan se update karo, warna purani value kho jaayegi.

qa.q: How do you choose the recurrence for a 1D DP?
qa.a: Answer 'what happens at index i?' for each possible choice. House Robber: either skip (take dp[i-1]) or rob (take dp[i-2] + nums[i]) — the max is the answer. Every 1D recurrence is 'the best of the choices, each expressed through earlier dp values'.

qa.q: Why is House Robber II solved by running rob twice?
qa.a: The circle breaks the linear dependency between house 0 and house n-1. Run the linear solution once excluding house 0 and once excluding house n-1, then take the max — one of those two choices must be optimal, and both are linear subproblems.

lessons.name: Unbounded Knapsack (Coin Change)
lessons.desc: Items can be reused any number of times. Coin Change (min coins) and Coin Change II (number of ways) are the templates — iterate amount first (unbounded) vs coins first (for ways, to avoid double-counting).
lessons.q: Why does the loop order differ between min-coins and ways?
lessons.qsub: When does unbounded DP degenerate into 0/1 (each item once)? · How do you recover WHICH coins were used? · What does dp[0] = 0 / dp[0] = 1 represent?
lessons.what:
Sikke hain 1, 5, 10 ke — aur har type jitni baar chaho use kar sakte ho, koi limit nahi. Isi ko unbounded kehte hain.

Do sawaal poochhe jaate hain aur dono alag hain: "kam se kam kitne sikke" (Coin Change) aur "kitne tarike" (Coin Change II).

Aur yahan wo cheez hai jo is topic ko tricky banati hai: dono ka code lagbhag same hai, farak sirf loop ke order ka hai — aur wo ek badlaav jawab poora badal deta hai.

Coins bahar, amount andar → har sikka ek hi baar consider hota hai → combinations (kram nahi ginta). Amount bahar, coins andar → har amount pe saare sikke dobara → permutations (kram bhi gina jaata hai).
lessons.analogy:
Dukaan pe sikke unlimited hain.
Agar tum ek sikke ko poora nipta ke agle pe jaate ho — "pehle saare 1 ke, phir saare 2 ke" — to {1,2} ek hi baar ginega.
Par agar har amount pe saare sikke dobara dekhte ho, to {1,2} aur {2,1} do alag jawab ban jaate hain.
lessons.why:
Loop order ka asar bahut subtle hai par jawab poora galat kar deta hai — aur code dekh ke bug pakadna mushkil hota hai. Isiliye interviewer ise pasand karta hai.

Test ye hai ki tum samajhte ho ki combinations aur permutations alag cheezein hain, aur ki loop ka order hi ye tay karta hai.

Doosra test: unbounded aur 0/1 ka farak. Unbounded mein loop aage chalta hai (kyunki reuse chahiye), 0/1 mein peeche (kyunki reuse nahi chahiye). Ye ek line poora topic badal deti hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Min coins: dp[a] = amount a ke liye kam se kam sikke. dp ko Infinity se bharo, dp[0] = 0.
2. Har amount pe har sikka try karo: dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1). Yahan loop order se koi farak nahi padta.
3. Aakhir mein dp[amount] abhi bhi Infinity hai? Matlab ban hi nahi sakta — -1 return karo.
4. Ways: dp[0] = 1 (khaali amount banane ka ek tarika — kuch mat lo).
5. Coins ka loop bahar rakho, amount andar. Isse har sikka sirf ek baar consider hota hai aur duplicate combinations nahi bante.
6. Unbounded mein amount ka loop aage (coin se amount tak) — isse dp[a - coin] mein wahi sikka dobara use ho sakta hai. Yahi reuse hai.

qa.q: Why does the loop order differ between min-coins and ways?
qa.a: For MIN coins, order doesn't matter (taking 1+2 or 2+1 costs the same), so amount-outer is fine. For WAYS, coins-outer treats combinations as sets — each coin is 'introduced' once, so [1,2] isn't counted as [2,1]. That's the difference between combinations and permutations.

qa.q: What's the recurrence for Coin Change?
qa.a: dp[a] = min over coins c of (dp[a - c] + 1). You pick one coin, reduce the amount by c, and ask for the best answer of the smaller amount — with unlimited reuse, the subproblem 'amount a-c' already allows reusing that coin.

lessons.name: 2D Grid DP
lessons.desc: dp[i][j] built from up (i-1, j) and left (i, j-1). Unique Paths and Minimum Path Sum are the templates — the grid's structure IS the dependency graph. Watch the boundary rows/columns.
lessons.q: How do you derive the recurrence for grid DP?
lessons.qsub: How do obstacle cells change the table? · What about diagonal or 8-direction movement? · Why do edge rows/cols get seeded to 1?
lessons.what:
Grid ke top-left pe khade ho, bottom-right tak jaana hai, aur sirf right ya down chal sakte ho. Kitne unique raaste hain? Ya sabse sasta raasta kaunsa hai?

Ab ulta socho. Kisi bhi cell (i, j) pe pahunche kaise? Sirf do jagah se — upar wale cell se neeche aake, ya left wale cell se right aake. Bas. Teesra koi raasta hai hi nahi.

Isliye dp[i][j] in dono se hi banta hai. Grid ki shakal hi dependency graph hai — tumhe sirf ye tay karna hai ki dono ko jodna hai (kitne raaste) ya min/max lena hai (kitni cost).

Pehli row aur pehli col alag se seed karni padti hai, kyunki wahan upar ya left kuch hai hi nahi.
lessons.analogy:
Ek building ka naksha socho jahan har flat tak sirf do tarike se pahuncha ja sakta hai — upar wale flat se seedhi utar ke, ya bagal wale flat se corridor paar karke.
To kisi bhi flat tak pahunchne ke total raaste = upar wale flat ke raaste + bagal wale flat ke raaste. Poori building dobara ghoomne ki zaroorat nahi — sirf do padosi kaafi hain.
lessons.why:
Ye pehla DP hai jahan state do numbers se banti hai, ek se nahi. Yahin se dp[i][j] wali soch shuru hoti hai jo LCS, Edit Distance aur knapsack — sab jagah chalti hai.

Aur ye sabse saaf jagah hai ye seekhne ki, kyunki state dikhai deti hai. Grid ka cell hi state hai — kuch imagine nahi karna padta.

Interview mein Unique Paths aur Minimum Path Sum warm-up questions hain. Inke baad seedha follow-up aata hai: “space kam kar sakte ho?” — aur rolling row ka jawab yahin se aata hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. dp[i][j] ka matlab ek line mein: “(0,0) se (i,j) tak ka jawab”.
2. Poocho: is cell tak aa kaise sakte the? Right/down movement ho to sirf up aur left.
3. Operator chuno — gin-ti ho to +, cost ho to min, profit ho to max.
4. Boundary seed karo: pehli row aur pehli col ke paas ek hi neighbour hai. Unique Paths mein sab 1, Min Path Sum mein running sum.
5. Loop upar se neeche, left se right — taaki dono neighbours pehle se bane hue milen.
6. Jawab dp[m-1][n-1] pe milega.
7. Space: sirf pichhli row chahiye? To ek hi row rakho aur usi ko left-to-right overwrite karte jao.

qa.q: How do you derive the recurrence for grid DP?
qa.a: Ask: how can you ARRIVE at cell (i,j)? For right/down moves, only from above (i-1,j) or left (i,j-1). Count problems SUM those ways; min/max problems take MIN of the two incoming costs, plus the cell's own value.

qa.q: How do you reduce 2D DP to O(cols) space?
qa.a: Each cell only reads its left neighbor (current row) and up-neighbor (previous row). So keep just the previous row — compute the new row left-to-right. You never touch rows older than the last one.

lessons.name: 2D Sequence DP (LCS / Edit Distance)
lessons.desc: Two strings/arrays compared cell by cell. dp[i][j] = answer for first i chars of A and first j chars of B. When chars match you diagonal-step; when they don't you take a min/max of the insert/delete/skip options.
lessons.q: Why the +1 sentinel row and column?
lessons.qsub: How do you recover the actual LCS, not just its length? · Why is Longest Palindromic Subsequence just LCS(s, reverse(s))? · When is space O(min(m,n)) achievable?
lessons.what:
Do strings hain aur inhe aapas mein compare karna hai — kitna common hai (LCS), ya ek ko doosri banane mein kitne kaam lagenge (Edit Distance).

dp[i][j] ka matlab: “A ke pehle i characters aur B ke pehle j characters ka jawab”. Poori strings nahi — sirf shuruaati hisse.

Ab har cell pe sirf ek sawaal hai — current do characters match karte hain?

Match: dono strings mein ek-ek kadam aage badho aur score +1. Ye tirchha (diagonal) cell hai.
Mismatch: ek taraf se ek character chhodna padega — ya A ka, ya B ka. Yahi upar aur left wale cells hain, aur unmein se best le lo.

Table (m+1) × (n+1) ka banta hai. Extra row aur col khaali string ke liye hai — yahi base case hai aur yahi if ke jhanjhat se bachata hai.
lessons.analogy:
Do dost apni-apni playlist ek saath sun rahe hain.
Gaana same aa gaya — dono khush, dono aage badh jaate hain, count +1.
Gaana alag aa gaya — ab kisi ek ko apna gaana skip karna padega. Do choice hain, aur jo aage jaake zyada match de wahi choice sahi hai.
Table bas ye saare faisle yaad rakh leta hai taaki dobara na sochna pade.
lessons.why:
LCS aur Edit Distance ek hi table ke do chehre hain, aur inhe seekhne ke baad poora ek parivaar khul jaata hai — Longest Palindromic Subsequence, Distinct Subsequences, Interleaving String, Regex Matching. Sab isi shakal ke hain.

Edit Distance to asli duniya mein hai: spell-check, git diff, DNA alignment, search bar ka “did you mean” — sab yahi algorithm chala rahe hain.

Aur interview mein ye check karta hai ki tum state define kar paate ho ya nahi. Agar dp[i][j] ka matlab shabdon mein bol sakte ho, to recurrence apne aap nikal aata hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Table (m+1) × (n+1) banao — extra row/col khaali string ke liye.
2. Base case bharo: LCS mein sab 0. Edit Distance mein pehli row = j aur pehli col = i (khaali se j characters banane mein j insert lagenge).
3. Har cell pe compare karo a[i-1] aur b[j-1] — minus one, kyunki table 1 se shuru hai aur string 0 se.
4. Match: LCS → 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]. Edit Distance → seedha dp[i-1][j-1] (koi kaam nahi).
5. Mismatch: LCS → max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Edit Distance → 1 + min(teeno padosi).
6. Jawab dp[m][n] pe — m-1 pe nahi, kyunki table 1-indexed hai.
7. Space: sirf pichhli row chahiye → do rows rakho, O(min(m, n)).
where: O(m × n) · space: O(m × n) or O(min(m,n))
O(m × n) · space: O(m × n) or O(n)

qa.q: Why the +1 sentinel row and column?
qa.a: dp[i][j] is 'first i of a vs first j of b'. With i=0 or j=0, the answer is the length of the other string (empty vs non-empty). Padding the table with an empty-string row/col gives clean base cases: LCS empty = 0; Edit Distance empty = j or i.

qa.q: What's the Edit Distance recurrence in words?
qa.a: If the current chars match, carry the diagonal answer. If not, it's 1 plus the cheapest of: delete a char (dp[i-1][j]), insert a char (dp[i][j-1]), or replace (dp[i-1][j-1]). The three operations ARE the three neighbor cells.

lessons.name: 0-1 Knapsack
lessons.desc: Each item is taken at most once — choose or skip. The capacity dimension makes it 2D: dp[i][w] = best value using first i items within weight w. Partition Equal Subset Sum and Target Sum are its classic LeetCode masks.
lessons.q: Why must the capacity loop run backward in 0/1 knapsack?
lessons.qsub: How does Target Sum map to knapsack (transform the equation)? · What's the difference between subset-sum and partition? · How do you recover WHICH items were chosen?
lessons.what:
Ek bag hai jiski weight limit fix hai, aur kuch items hain — har item ka apna weight aur value. Har item sirf ek baar le sakte ho. Max value kitni bhar sakte ho?

Har item pe sirf do choice hai — lo ya chhodo. Isiliye naam 0/1.

dp[i][w] = “pehle i items mein se, w weight ke andar best value”. Do dimensions chahiye kyunki dono cheezein badal rahi hain: kaunsa item dekh rahe ho, aur kitni jagah bachi hai.

Ab yahan sabse zaroori baat, jo poore topic ka dil hai. Jab tum dp ko ek hi 1D array mein squeeze karte ho, to capacity ka loop ulta (peeche se) chalana padta hai. Aage se chalaoge to dp[w - wt] mein wahi item pehle se ghusa hua milega — aur item do baar chala jaayega. Bas yahi ek line 0/1 aur unbounded ka farq hai.
lessons.analogy:
Shaadi ke buffet mein ek hi thaali hai aur har dish sirf ek baar mil rahi hai.
Ab agar tum khaali jagah ke hisaab se chhoti se badi plate bharte jaoge, to jo dish abhi-abhi rakhi thi wahi dobara ginne lagogi.
Isliye ulta chalo — sabse badi jagah pehle bharo. Tab jo dekh rahe ho wo hamesha is dish se pehle wali plate hoti hai.
lessons.why:
Ye pattern LeetCode pe apne asli naam se kabhi nahi aata. Wo Partition Equal Subset Sum, Target Sum, Last Stone Weight II, Ones and Zeroes ban ke aata hai — aur agar knapsack pehchan liya to teeno ek jaise ban jaate hain.

Aur backward-loop wala trick DP ka sabse important “kyun” hai. Agar ye samajh gaye, to tumhe recurrence ratne ki zaroorat hi nahi padegi — tum khud derive kar loge ki loop kis taraf jaana chahiye.

Interviewer aksar yahi poochta hai: “loop ulta kyun hai?” — ye sirf ek line hai, par isse pata chal jaata hai ki tumne DP samjha hai ya template ratta maara hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Pehchano: subset chunna hai + koi capacity/target hai + item repeat nahi ho sakta → 0/1 knapsack.
2. State: dp[w] = “w weight tak best value” (ya boolean — “w banaya ja sakta hai kya”).
3. Seed: dp[0] = 0 (ya true). Khaali bag hamesha valid hai — ye seed bhoolna sabse common bug hai.
4. Bahar wala loop items ka.
5. Andar wala loop capacity ka, peeche se: for (w = cap; w ≥ wt; w--).
6. dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - wt] + val) — chhodo ya lo.
7. Subset Sum mein: value ki jagah boolean, dp[w] = dp[w] || dp[w - num].
8. Partition: total odd hai to seedha false. Warna target = total / 2 pe subset-sum chala do.

qa.q: Why must the capacity loop run backward in 0/1 knapsack?
qa.a: dp[w] should consider each item once. Going forward, dp[w - x] might already include the current item (updated earlier in the same loop) — that's unlimited reuse. Backward means dp[w - x] is still the previous item's value, so the item is used at most once.

qa.q: How do you recognize a knapsack problem?
qa.a: A subset-selection constraint with a capacity-like bound: 'subset sums to target', 'can we fit items under weight W with max value'. If items are limited to one use each → 0/1; reusable → unbounded; ordered arrangements → different dimension.

lessons.name: State Machine DP
lessons.desc: Track multiple STATES of ownership/position per day — for Buy/Sell Stock, whether you currently hold a share. dp[i][state] where state ∈ {not holding, holding}. Transitions model buy/sell/hold decisions.
lessons.q: What does 'state' mean in state-machine DP?
lessons.qsub: What does the cooldown state add? · Why start hold at -Infinity? · When is the single-pass min-so-far solution enough?
lessons.what:
Stock ki roz ki keemat di hai. Kharido, becho, ya kuch mat karo — max profit kitna?

Yahan sirf dp[i] = “din i tak max profit” likhoge to phas jaoge. Kyunki agla faisla ek aur baat pe depend karta hai jo is number mein hai hi nahi: abhi tumhare paas stock hai ya nahi?

Agar stock paas hai to aaj tum bech sakte ho. Nahi hai to kharid sakte ho. Options hi alag hain.

Isliye state mein wo baat daal do. dp[i][0] = stock nahi hai wala best, dp[i][1] = stock hai wala best. Ab har din har state ke paas do hi raaste hain — wahi rehne do, ya doosre state se switch karo (kharid ke ya bech ke).

Bas yahi pattern hai. Aur ye scale bhi karta hai — cooldown ho to teesra state jodo, k transactions ho to ek aur dimension.
lessons.analogy:
Ek sabzi wala socho. Roz subah wo do haalaton mein se kisi ek mein hota hai — maal khareeda hua paas hai, ya jeb mein sirf paisa hai.
Dono haalaton mein uske aage ke options bilkul alag hain: maal hai to bech sakta hai, paisa hai to khareed sakta hai.
Isliye uska hisaab-kitab ek number nahi, do numbers rakhta hai — "aaj tak ka best, agar maal paas hai" aur "aaj tak ka best, agar nahi hai".
lessons.why:
Poora Buy and Sell Stock parivaar (I, II, III, IV, cooldown, fee) — chhe alag-alag LeetCode problems — ek hi saanche se ban jaate hain. Sirf states ki ginti badalti hai, soch wahi rehti hai.

Aur isse zyada important: ye sikhata hai ki state kaise badhaayi jaati hai. Jab tumhara DP kaam na kare, aksar wajah yahi hoti hai ki koi zaroori baat state mein daali hi nahi gayi. Ye topic wahi reflex banata hai.

Interview mein ye bahut aam follow-up chain hai: pehle simple version, phir “ab cooldown add karo”, phir “ab at most k transactions”. State machine wale ke liye teeno ek hi cheez hain.

Kaise sochein:

1. States likho — kaunsi baat aage ke options badalti hai? Stock hai / nahi. Cooldown ho to teesra: aaj becha hai.
2. Har state ke transitions likho — is state se kahan-kahan ja sakte ho, aur uski keemat kya hai.
3. Seed karo: cash = 0 (kuch nahi kiya), hold = -Infinity (bina kharide hold karna namumkin hai). Yahan 0 likhna sabse aam bug hai.
4. Har din dono states update karo. Dono lines ko purani values chahiye — isliye cash pehle update karo, ya pehle copy le lo.
5. Aakhir mein jawab cash hai — hold nahi. Haath mein stock rakh ke profit nahi ginta.
6. Fee? Bechte waqt ghata do. Cooldown? Teesra state. k transactions? k ki dimension jodo.

qa.q: What does 'state' mean in state-machine DP?
qa.a: The condition that changes your options — holding vs not holding a share. dp[holding] and dp[cash] evolve day by day: each can 'stay' or 'transition'. Any flag that gates decisions (cooldown, transaction limit) is another state dimension.

qa.q: How does the k-transaction version change?
qa.a: Add k as a dimension: dp[k][holding] vs dp[k][cash]. Buying moves you to the next transaction count. The same transition logic applies, just indexed by how many trades you've used.

lessons.name: Interval DP
lessons.desc: dp[i][j] describes a segment from i to j. The answer for a segment combines answers of smaller segments split at some k. The canonical shapes: longest palindromic substring/subsequence and burst-balloon-style 'choose the last to act'.
lessons.q: How do you know interval DP applies?
lessons.qsub: How does palindromic subsequence use LCS? · What makes burst-balloon O(n³)? · When is expand-around-center better than table DP?
lessons.what:
Ab tak dp[i] ka matlab tha “ek point tak ka jawab”. Interval DP mein dp[i][j] ka matlab hai “poore tukde [i..j] ka jawab” — ek range, ek point nahi.

Aur yahan twist hai. Chhote segments se bada segment seedha nahi banta. Tumhe range ke andar ek split point k chunna padta hai, aur dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] ko jodna padta hai — plus us split pe jo cost ya value banti hai wo bhi.

Kaunsa k sahi hai? Pata nahi. Isliye saare try karo, best rakh lo. Yahi O(n³) ki wajah hai.

Aur ek zaroori baat: dp[i][j] ko apne andar ke chhote segments chahiye. Isliye table lambai ke kram mein bharna padta hai — pehle len 1, phir len 2, phir len 3. Seedha i aur j pe loop chalaya to aadhe-bane cells padh loge.
lessons.analogy:
Ek lambi chocolate bar todni hai aur har cut ki apni cost hai.
Sawaal ye hai ki pehla cut kahan lagayein — kyunki uske baad do chhoti bars ka hisaab alag-alag chalega.
Kaunsa cut sahi hai ye pehle se pata nahi chalta, isliye har jagah cut karke dekho aur jo total sabse sasta pade wahi rakh lo.
lessons.why:
Ye aakhri classic DP shape hai. 1D, 2D grid, 2D sequence, knapsack — in sabme state ek ya do points se banti thi. Yahan state ek range hai, aur transition ek split hai. Ye soch alag hai aur seekhni padti hai.

Burst Balloons is category ka sabse famous interview question hai, aur wo isliye mushkil hai ki log pehla kaunsa balloon phodun sochte hain. Sahi soch ulti hai — aakhri kaunsa phodun. Tab dono taraf ke segments swatantra ho jaate hain.

Matrix Chain Multiplication, Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick, Palindrome Partitioning — sab isi ek soch ke roop hain.

Kaise sochein:

1. dp[i][j] ka matlab likho — “segment [i..j] ka best jawab”.
2. Base case: len = 1 (aur palindrome mein len = 2 bhi) haath se bharo.
3. Bahar wala loop LENGTH ka — for (len = 2; len ≤ n; len++). Ye sabse zaroori line hai.
4. Andar i chalao, aur j = i + len - 1 nikaal lo.
5. Sabse andar k chalao i se j-1 tak — har split try karo.
6. dp[i][j] = best(dp[i][j], dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + cost).
7. Burst Balloons ka twist: k ko “pehla” nahi, “aakhri phoodne wala” maano. Tab dono taraf alag-alag ho jaate hain aur padosi fix rehte hain.
8. Jawab dp[0][n-1] pe — poora segment.

qa.q: How do you know interval DP applies?
qa.a: The answer is defined over a contiguous range [i, j] and decomposes by splitting into smaller ranges — a palindrome [i,j] is a palindrome iff s[i]===s[j] AND [i+1,j-1] is a palindrome. The 'segment built from sub-segments' structure is the signature.

qa.q: Why expand around center for palindromic substring?
qa.a: There are 2n-1 centers (each char + each gap). Expanding each takes O(n), total O(n²) time and O(1) space — beating the O(n²) space DP for SUBSTRING (contiguous). The DP table only wins when you need the palindromic SUBSEQUENCE, which isn't contiguous.

lessons.name: DP with Bitmasks
lessons.desc: When the state includes which elements are used, encode it as an integer bitmask: bit i set means item i is taken. Combined with memo, this handles subset-partition, TSP, and assignment problems in O(2^n * n) — exponential but often the intended answer for n <= 20.
lessons.q: When do you recognize bitmask DP is the tool?
lessons.qsub: How do you check if bit i is set in mask? · How do you add item i to the mask? · Why does n have to be small? · How do you prune a partition DP for speed?
lessons.what:
Kabhi-kabhi state mein ye rakhna padta hai ki kaun-kaun se items abhi tak use ho chuke hain — sirf kitne nahi, balki kaunse.

Ab wo set ko kisi array ya Set mein rakh ke memo ki key banana mushkil hai. Lekin agar items kam hain (n ≤ 20), to poora set ek hi integer mein fit ho jaata hai.

Har bit ek item hai. Bit i agar 1 hai → item i use ho chuka. 1011 ka matlab: items 0, 1 aur 3 liye ja chuke hain, item 2 bacha hai. Ye number hai 11 — aur wahi tumhari array index ban jaata hai.

Asli faayda ye hai: alag-alag kram se aaya hua wahi set ek hi state ban jaata hai. Isliye n! permutations ghatt ke 2ⁿ subsets reh jaate hain. Exponential to phir bhi hai, par 2²⁰ = 10 lakh — ye chalta hai. 20! = 24 lakh crore — ye nahi.
lessons.analogy:
Bus ki booking chart socho — har seat ke saamne ek dabba, bhara ya khaali.
Poori bus ki haalat bataane ke liye tumhe seat numbers ki list nahi chahiye, bas ek line kaafi hai: 1011.
Aur do log jinhone alag-alag kram mein wahi seats book ki — unki chart bilkul same dikhegi. Yahi wo cheez hai jo kaam aadha kar deti hai.
lessons.why:
Ye topic tumhe ek naya hathiyaar deta hai: jab state ek set ho, to use ek integer bana do. Ye trick sirf DP mein nahi — graph, backtracking aur state-space search — har jagah kaam aati hai.

Aur ek bahut practical signal: agar problem ki constraints mein n ≤ 20 ya n ≤ 15 likha hai, to ye lagbhag hamesha bitmask ka ishaara hota hai. Itni chhoti limit poly-time solution ke liye zaroori hi nahi hoti — wo isliye di gayi hai kyunki intended solution exponential hai.

Travelling Salesman, Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets, Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes — teeno interview mein aate hain aur teeno yahi pattern hain.

Kaise sochein:

1. n dekho. n ≤ 20 ho tabhi aage badho.
2. Har item ko ek bit do — item i → bit i.
3. State likho: dp[mask], ya dp[mask][last] agar ye bhi maayne rakhta ho ki aakhri kaunsa liya tha (jaise TSP mein).
4. Base case: mask = 0 (kuch nahi liya) ya mask = (1 << n) - 1 (sab liya).
5. Transition: har unused item try karo — if (!(mask & (1 << i))) → naya mask mask | (1 << i).
6. Memo lagao — array of size 1 << n. Map se tez, kyunki key already integer hai.
7. Prune karo: partition problems mein items ulta sort karo (bada pehle), duplicates skip karo, aur target cross hote hi return kar do. Isse practical speed kai guna badh jaati hai.

qa.q: When do you recognize bitmask DP is the tool?
qa.a: The state is "which items are used" and n <= ~20. If the same used-set can recur through different orders, memoizing on the mask collapses all those orders into one state.

qa.q: Why is it O(2^n * n) rather than O(n!)?
qa.a: Bitmask DP merges all permutations with the same used-set into a single state. n! orderings collapse to 2^n subsets, each considering n next choices — that is the whole win.

lessons.name: Digit DP
lessons.desc: Counts integers in a range [0, N] satisfying digit constraints (e.g. no consecutive 1s, only digits from a set, not exceeding N). The state is (position, tight, extra flags): tight means the prefix already equals N's prefix, so the current digit is capped.
lessons.q: What does the "tight" flag actually do?
lessons.qsub: How do you compute f(L, R) from f(N)? · Why is tight only a boolean, not a range? · What changes for properties like digit sums? · When would you need a "started" flag?
lessons.what:
Sawaal aisa hai: “0 se N tak kitne numbers hain jinme koi digit repeat nahi hota?” Aur N hai 10¹⁸. Ek-ek number check karna namumkin hai.

Digit DP ka poora idea ye hai: number ko ek value ki tarah mat dekho, use digits ki ek line ki tarah dekho jo tum left se right bana rahe ho. Numbers crore mein hain, par digits sirf 19 hain.

Ab har position pe ek hi sawaal hai — yahan kaunsa digit rakh sakta hoon? Aur iska jawab ek flag se aata hai: tight.

tight ON ka matlab hai ki ab tak jo digits rakhe hain wo N ke digits ke bilkul barabar hain. Aise mein current digit N ke digit se zyada nahi ho sakta — warna number N se bada ho jaayega. Par jaise hi tumne ek chhota digit rakh diya, number pakka N se chhota hai — aur uske baad har position pe 0 se 9 tak sab khula hai. tight phir kabhi wapas ON nahi hota.
lessons.analogy:
Odometer pe number set kar rahe ho, ek-ek dial ghumaake, aur limit hai N.
Jab tak har dial theek N wale digit pe hai, tum kinare pe chal rahe ho — agla dial N se aage nahi ghuma sakte.
Par ek baar koi dial thoda peeche set kar diya, to tum kinare se hatt gaye — ab baaki saare dials jitna marzi ghumao, number N se chhota hi rahega.
lessons.why:
Ye Phase 7 ka sabse specialised topic hai, aur saaf-saaf batana zaroori hai: ye typical product-company interview mein bahut kam aata hai. Competitive programming aur kuch hard LeetCode problems mein zaroor aata hai.

Par ek badi cheez sikhata hai jo har jagah kaam aati hai: state mein ek flag daal ke poori range ka constraint sambhal lena. tight ek boolean hai jo “kya main abhi bhi upper limit pe chal raha hoon” poora sawaal encode kar deta hai.

Aur ek reusable trick: range ko ghatane se nikalo — answer(L..R) = f(R) - f(L-1). Ye prefix sums se lekar digit DP tak, har jagah chalti hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. N ko string bana lo — ab positions pe kaam karoge.
2. State likho: (pos, tight, started, problem ka apna flag).
3. Har position pe limit nikalo: tight ho to N[pos] tak, warna 9 tak.
4. Har allowed digit d pe recursion karo. Naya tight = tight && (d === limit).
5. Base case: pos === N.length → yahan tay karo ki ye number ginti mein aata hai ya nahi.
6. Memo: sirf tab jab tight aur started dono off hon. Kyunki tight wale raaste unique hote hain — unhe cache karna galat hai.
7. Range: f(R) - f(L-1).
8. Leading zeros: started flag rakho — pehle non-zero digit se pehle wale zeroes ko digit mat gino.

qa.q: What does the "tight" flag actually do?
qa.a: It encodes whether the digits chosen so far exactly match N's prefix. If yes, the current digit must not exceed N's digit (and if it equals it, tight stays on). Once any digit is smaller, everything later is free.

qa.q: How do you handle leading zeros?
qa.a: Add a "started" flag: zeros before the first nonzero digit do not count as digits. Enable it once a nonzero digit is placed, then allow zeros normally.

lessons.name: Heap / Priority Queue
lessons.desc: A binary tree stored in an array that keeps the min (or max) at the root. Insert and extract-min are O(log n), peek is O(1). The tool for 'top k' and 'smallest/largest/closest' problems. JS has no built-in heap — write one or polyfill via a priority queue.
lessons.q: Why is a heap better than sorting for top-k?
lessons.qsub: What's the difference between min-heap and priority queue? · How do you implement a max-heap in JS? · Why is heapify O(n) instead of O(n log n)?
lessons.what:
Ek badi list hai aur tumhe baar-baar sirf sabse chhota (ya sabse bada) chahiye — aur beech-beech mein naye items bhi aate rehte hain. Poori list sort karna barbaadi hai, kyunki tumhe poora order chahiye hi nahi.

Heap ek aisa structure hai jo sirf ek guarantee deta hai: root pe hamesha sabse chhota (ya bada) baitha hai. Bas. Bhai-behno ka aapas mein koi order nahi. Isi kam guarantee ki wajah se ye itna sasta hai.

Dikhne mein binary tree hai, par store array mein hota hai — index i ke children 2i+1 aur 2i+2 pe milte hain. Koi pointer nahi, koi node object nahi.

peek O(1), push aur pop O(log n) — kyunki tree ki height log n hai aur element bas usi raste pe upar ya neeche khisakta hai.
lessons.analogy:
Emergency ward ki line socho. Wahan poori line serious-ness ke order mein nahi lagi hoti — bas itna pakka hai ki sabse critical patient sabse aage hai.
Naya critical case aaya to wo aage khisak jaata hai, baaki thoda peeche ho jaate hain — poori line dobara nahi lagti.
lessons.why:
“Top k” wale sawaal interview mein bahut aam hain — Kth Largest, Top K Frequent, K Closest Points, Merge k Sorted Lists. Inka naive jawab sort karna hai (O(n log n)), heap wala jawab O(n log k).

Aur ek badi baat: heap stream pe kaam karta hai. Data aata rahe, tum har waqt answer de sakte ho. Sorting ko har baar shuru se karna padega.

JS mein heap built-in nahi hai — isliye interviewer aksar dekhna chahta hai ki tum ek chhota sa heap khud likh sakte ho ya nahi. Ye likhna aana chahiye, sirf naam jaanna kaafi nahi.

Kaise sochein:

1. Array mein rakho. parent(i) = (i-1) >> 1, children(i) = 2i+1, 2i+2.
2. push: end mein daalo, phir jab tak parent bada hai — swap karke upar chadho (siftUp).
3. pop: root uthao, aakhri element ko root pe rakho, phir chhote wale child ke saath swap karke neeche utro (siftDown).
4. Max-heap chahiye? Do tareeke — comparator ulta kar do, ya values ka minus daal do.
5. Top k ka ulta niyam: k sabse bade chahiye → size k ka min-heap rakho. Naya element root se bada ho tabhi andar lo, aur root nikaal do.
6. Size k se bada mat hone do — yahi O(n log k) deta hai.
7. Ties: priority barabar ho to ek counter ya doosra key laga do, warna order random rahega.

qa.q: Why is a heap better than sorting for top-k?
qa.a: A size-k heap is O(n log k) — for k much smaller than n that beats O(n log n) sorting. And a heap handles a live stream of items; sorting must restart from scratch each time. When k ≈ n, sorting wins on constant factors.

qa.q: How do you find the median of a data stream with heaps?
qa.a: Keep a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, balanced in size. Median is the max of the lower heap (odd count) or the average of both roots (even). Each insert rebalances in O(log n) — see the Two Heaps lesson.

lessons.name: Heap Variations
lessons.desc: The two heaps pattern (median of a stream), k-way merge, and lazy deletion (mark-and-sweep stale entries). These variations turn the basic heap into a solution for 'Find Median from Data Stream', 'Merge k Sorted Lists', and scheduling problems.
lessons.q: How does the two-heap median pattern work?
lessons.qsub: When does the two-heap trick fail? · What's the running time of k-way merge vs merging one by one? · Why does Task Scheduler need the cooldown-aware reinsert?
lessons.what:
Basic heap sirf ek kaam jaanta hai — “sabse chhota do”. Par asli problems isse thoda aage maangti hain. Teen variations sab kuch cover kar dete hain.

1. K-way merge. k sorted lists ko ek mein milana hai. Heap mein har list ka sirf current pehla element rakho. Sabse chhota nikaalo, output mein daalo, aur usi list ka agla element heap mein push kar do. Heap kabhi k se bada nahi hota — isliye O(n log k).

2. Lazy deletion. Heap se beech ka element hatana O(n) hai. Isliye hataate hi nahi — use “stale” mark kar dete ho, aur jab wo root pe aaye tab chup-chaap discard kar dete ho.

3. Count phir heapify. Task Scheduler jaisi problems mein pehle frequency gino, phir max-heap banao, ek chalao, aur cooldown ke baad wapas push kar do.
lessons.analogy:
Station pe 10 platforms se trains aa rahi hain aur tumhe ek single arrival board banana hai.
Tum saari trains ki list nahi dekhte — sirf har platform ki agli train dekhte ho, unme se jo sabse pehle aa rahi hai use board pe likhte ho, aur phir usi platform ki uske baad wali train check karte ho.
Board pe kabhi bhi sirf 10 entries hoti hain, chahe kul trains hazaar hon.
lessons.why:
Ye teeno LeetCode ke bade sawaalon mein seedha aate hain — Merge k Sorted Lists (hard), Task Scheduler, Sliding Window Median, Smallest Range Covering K Lists.

Aur ek soch sikhata hai jo aage bhi kaam aati hai: jab data structure tumhe wo operation nahi de raha jo chahiye, to structure badalne ke bajaye problem ko us structure ke hisaab se mod do. Lazy deletion isi ka sabse saaf example hai — delete nahi kar sakte? To delete karo hi mat, bas ignore karna seekh lo.

External sorting (jo data RAM mein fit nahi hota) bhi asal mein k-way merge hi hai — ye system design mein bhi aa jaata hai.

Kaise sochein:

K-way merge:
1. Har list ka pehla element heap mein daalo, saath mein [value, listIndex, pos].
2. Sabse chhota nikaalo → output.
3. Usi list ka agla element push karo (agar bacha ho). Khatam hone tak dohrao.

Lazy deletion:
4. Ek Set ya counter rakho "kaun-kaun hataya ja chuka hai".
5. pop se pehle while loop chalao — jab tak root stale hai, use phenkte raho.
6. Asli size = heap size − stale count.

Task Scheduler:
7. Frequency gino, max-heap banao.
8. Ek round mein n+1 tak alag-alag tasks nikaalo, phir jinme count bacha hai unhe wapas push karo.
where: O(log n) per insert · space: O(n)

qa.q: How does the two-heap median pattern work?
qa.a: The lower half lives in a max-heap, the upper in a min-heap, sizes differ by at most 1. Insert: add to lower, then shift the max into upper to keep the invariant. Median = lower's max when sizes are unequal, else average of both roots.

qa.q: What is lazy deletion and when do you need it?
qa.a: Heaps only expose the root for removal. To 'remove' an arbitrary element, mark it stale (a tombstone) and filter it out when it surfaces as the root. Standard for Task Scheduler and 'max heap with update' patterns where real deletion would cost O(n).

lessons.name: Backtracking
lessons.desc: Systematic exhaustive search over choices: make a choice, recurse, then UNDO it. One template covers subsets, permutations, combinations, and board search. Prune early to avoid exploring dead branches.
lessons.q: What's the ONE template behind all backtracking?
lessons.qsub: When is backtracking the right tool vs DP? · How do you prune board search (Word Search) early? · Why must you copy the path before pushing it?
lessons.what:
Kuch sawaal “best kya hai” nahi poochte — wo poochte hain “saare tarike batao”. Saare subsets, saari permutations, saare valid boards. Yahan koi shortcut nahi hai — sabko dekhna hi padega. Sirf ye zaroori hai ki tarike se dekho, aur galat raaste jaldi chhod do.

Backtracking teen kadam hai, aur bas teen:

1. Choose — ek option lo, path mein daal do.
2. Explore — baaki decisions pe recursion chalao.
3. Unchoose — wo option wapas nikaal lo (path.pop()).

Teesra kadam hi asli hai. Agar tumne wapas nahi nikaala, to bhai wali branch tumhare kachre ke saath shuru hogi — aur answers galat aayenge. Yahi backtracking ka sabse aam bug hai.

Aur ek cheez jo mediocre solution ko accha banati hai: pruning. Jo branch pakka fail hone wali hai, wahin return kar do — poori sub-tree bach jaati hai.
lessons.analogy:
Bhool-bhulaiya mein jaate waqt har mod pe chalk se nishaan lagate jao.
Dead-end mila? Wapas aao aur apna nishaan mita do — warna agli baar us raste pe aake lagega ki yahan pehle hi aa chuke ho.
Nishaan mitana hi path.pop() hai.
lessons.why:
Ye poore ek parivaar ka ek hi taala-chaabi hai. Subsets, Subsets II, Permutations, Permutations II, Combination Sum I/II/III, Palindrome Partitioning, Letter Combinations, N-Queens, Sudoku Solver, Word Search — sabme wahi teen line hai. Sirf pruning aur base case badalte hain.

Isliye ye seekhne pe return bahut zyada hai. Ek template pakka karo, aur ek dozen interview questions khul jaate hain.

Aur interviewer ye bhi dekhta hai ki tum complexity honestly bol paate ho ya nahi. O(n × 2ⁿ) bolna — aur ye samajhna ki n ka factor answer copy karne se aata hai — ye chhoti si baat bahut farq daalti hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Poocho: har step pe choices kya hain? Aur kab ruk jaana hai?
2. Ek path array rakho jo abhi tak ke choices rakhta hai.
3. Base case: path poora ho gaya? To res.push([...path]) — copy karke, warna sab entries ek hi (khaali) array ka reference ban jaayengi.
4. Har choice pe teen line: push → recurse → pop.
5. Repeat rokna: combinations mein start index aage badhao; permutations mein used[] array rakho.
6. Duplicates: pehle sort karo, phir if (i > start && a[i] === a[i-1]) continue.
7. Prune: sum target se paar? Board invalid? Wahin return — aage ki poori sub-tree bach gayi.

qa.q: What's the ONE template behind all backtracking?
qa.a: Choose → explore → unchoose. Build the answer incrementally, recurse on the remaining decisions, then undo the last choice so sibling branches start from the same state. Subsets, permutations, combinations, and board search all fit it — only the pruning differs.

qa.q: How do you avoid duplicates (Subsets II, Permutations II)?
qa.a: Sort the input first, then skip a value when it equals the previous one AND the previous occurrence wasn't used at this level: if (i > start && nums[i] === nums[i-1]) continue. This prunes sibling branches that would produce identical results.

lessons.name: Greedy
lessons.desc: Make the locally optimal choice at each step, hoping it yields the global optimum. Greedy only works when a proof (or strong intuition) shows local choices can't block a better global outcome. Interval scheduling and jump-game are the classics.
lessons.q: How do you know a greedy is correct?
lessons.qsub: Why does sorting by end maximize non-overlapping intervals? · When does the two-pointer greedy fail? · How would you disprove a greedy with a counterexample?
lessons.what:
Greedy ka matlab hai: har step pe wo choice lo jo abhi sabse acchi lag rahi hai, aur peeche mud ke mat dekho. Koi table nahi, koi recursion nahi — ek pass mein kaam khatam.

Jab ye chalta hai to sabse saaf aur sabse tez solution hota hai. Problem sirf ek hai: ye aksar chalta nahi hai, aur jab nahi chalta to koi error nahi aata — bas jawab galat aata hai.

Isliye greedy ka asli kaam code likhna nahi, ye tay karna hai ki greedy chalega ya nahi.

Do tareeke hain. Exchange argument: maano optimal answer ne pehle step pe kuch aur kiya — ab usko greedy wali choice se badal do. Agar answer kabhi kharab nahi hota, to greedy sahi hai. Ya counterexample: ek chhota sa input dhoondo jahan greedy fail ho jaaye. Mil gaya? To greedy nahi chalega — DP nikaalo.
lessons.analogy:
Ek hi hall mein poore din ki meetings fit karni hain — zyada se zyada meetings.
Instinct kehta hai jo pehle shuru ho use pehle lo. Galat — ek subah 9 baje shuru hoke shaam 6 baje khatam hone wali meeting poora din kha jaayegi.
Sahi rule hai: jo jaldi khatam ho use pehle lo. Hall jitni jaldi khaali hoga, utni zyada meetings ghusengi.
lessons.why:
Interviewer greedy isliye deta hai kyunki ye sabse aam galti hai. Log DP wali problem pe greedy laga dete hain, 5 test case pass ho jaate hain, aur chhathe pe fail. Wo dekhna chahta hai ki tum pehle soch rahe ho ya seedha likh rahe ho.

Aur jab greedy sahi hota hai, to wo O(n log n) ya O(n) deta hai jahan DP O(n²) leta — ye bada farq hai.

Interval problems (Merge Intervals, Non-overlapping Intervals, Meeting Rooms) aur reachability problems (Jump Game, Gas Station) bahut common hain, aur inka intended solution greedy hi hai.

Ek line jo interview mein bahut acchi lagti hai: “Main pehle ye check kar leta hoon ki greedy safe hai ya nahi — agar exchange argument banta hai to greedy, warna DP.”

Kaise sochein:

1. Greedy rule likho — "har step pe main ye chunuga".
2. Test karo: 3-4 chhote inputs pe haath se chalao. Fail ho gaya? Mubarak ho — DP jaana pad gaya, par 20 minute bach gaye.
3. Saabit karo: exchange argument — optimal ki pehli choice ko apni choice se badlo, aur dekho answer kharab hota hai ya nahi.
4. Sort key sabse important hai. Non-overlapping intervals → end se sort. Merge intervals → start se sort. Ye ulta kiya to sab galat.
5. Ek "best-so-far" variable rakho — sabse door pahunch (Jump Game), current end (scheduling), running sum (Gas Station).
6. Ek hi pass mein chalao. Peeche mudna pade to greedy tha hi nahi.
7. Complexity aksar sort ki wajah se O(n log n) ho jaati hai.
where: O(n log n) or O(n) · space: O(n)

qa.q: How do you know a greedy is correct?
qa.a: Write the exchange argument: if the optimal solution does something different from the greedy at this step, swapping in the greedy choice never worsens the result. Interval scheduling's proof — replacing the first picked interval with the earliest-ending one always works — is the model to imitate.

qa.q: Greedy vs DP — how do you decide fast?
qa.a: If the 'locally best' choice always stays optimal regardless of future input → greedy. If later decisions can undo earlier ones, or the future depends on accumulated choices (subsets, paths) → DP. When unsure, a single counterexample settles it; DP is the safe fallback.

lessons.name: Monotonic Stack
lessons.desc: A stack that stays strictly increasing or decreasing. Pop elements that break the invariant, then push. Because each element pushes and pops once, it's O(n) — the answer to 'next greater/smaller' and 'largest rectangle' family problems.
lessons.q: When is the answer computed — push or pop?
lessons.qsub: How do you handle circular arrays (Next Greater II)? · What's the invariant that makes it O(n)? · Why store indices and not values?
lessons.what:
Phase 1 mein monotonic stack se next greater nikaala tha. Yahan wahi cheez ek kadam aage jaati hai — ab har element ke dono kinare chahiye, aur unse ek area ya contribution banta hai.

Largest Rectangle in Histogram sochlo. Har bar ke liye sawaal ye hai: ye bar kitni door tak apni poori height pe faili reh sakti hai? Jawab do cheezon se aata hai — left mein pehli chhoti bar kahan hai, aur right mein pehli chhoti bar kahan hai.

Monotonic stack dono ek hi pass mein de deta hai. Jis waqt koi element pop hota hai, us waqt do baatein ek saath pata chal jaati hain: current element uska right kinara hai, aur pop ke baad jo naya top bacha wo uska left kinara hai.

Isliye yahan sabse zaroori niyam ye hai: answer push pe nahi, pop pe banta hai. Push to sirf hisaab-kitab hai.
lessons.analogy:
Ek building ke saamne khade ho aur poochte ho ki uska view kitni door tak khula hai.
Jawab tab tak nahi milta jab tak dono taraf ek-ek oonchi building na mil jaaye.
Left wali to pehle se pata thi. Right wali jis din mil gayi, us din us building ka poora hisaab ek saath ho jaata hai — aur wo list se hata di jaati hai.
lessons.why:
Ye poora parivaar “hard” tag ke saath aata hai aur ek hi trick pe chalta hai — Largest Rectangle in Histogram, Maximal Rectangle, Sum of Subarray Minimums, Trapping Rain Water, Next Greater Element II.

Naive solution O(n²) hai aur wo bade inputs pe TLE dega. Monotonic stack O(n) deta hai — aur is farq ko samjha ke bol paana interview mein bada point hai.

Aur ye ek soch sikhata hai jo aage kaam aati hai: har element ka contribution alag se gino. Sum of Subarray Minimums mein tum saare subarrays nahi ghoomte — tum har element se poochte ho "tum kitne subarrays ke minimum ho?" aur wahi count kinaron se nikal aata hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Tay karo stack increasing rakhna hai ya decreasing. Largest Rectangle mein increasing (heights badhti hui).
2. Stack mein indices daalo, values nahi — width nikaalne ke liye position chahiye.
3. Har naye element pe: jab tak stack ka top order tod raha hai, pop karo — aur har pop pe us element ka answer likh do.
4. Width formula: i - stack[top] - 1. Yahan stack[top] pop ke baad ka top hai — yahi left kinara hai.
5. Stack mein shuru mein -1 sentinel daal do — index 0 wale case ka if apne aap khatam ho jaata hai.
6. Aakhir mein bache hue elements ko bhi pop karo — unka right kinara array ka end hai. (Ya heights ke aakhir mein ek 0 jod do.)
7. Circular? Loop 2n tak chalao aur index i % n use karo, par push sirf pehle chakkar mein karo.

qa.q: When is the answer computed — push or pop?
qa.a: Compute on POP. When the current element pops a stack top, the current element IS the 'next greater' (or the right boundary for histograms) of the popped element. Pushing is just bookkeeping; the pop is where the information is revealed.

qa.q: Why does the histogram use a sentinel -1?
qa.a: The rectangle's width is i - leftBound - 1, where leftBound is the new stack top after popping. A -1 sentinel makes that formula work even when the popped bar's left bound is the array's very start — no special-casing index 0.

lessons.name: Two Heaps
lessons.desc: A max-heap for the smaller half and a min-heap for the larger half, balanced to a size difference of at most one. Gives O(log n) insert and O(1) median peek — the canonical answer for 'Find Median from Data Stream'.
lessons.q: Why does this stay balanced?
lessons.qsub: How does sliding-window median use lazy deletion? · What breaks if the heaps use different comparators? · Why is low allowed to be one element bigger but not high?
lessons.what:
Numbers ek-ek karke aa rahe hain aur har naye number ke baad turant median batana hai. Har baar sort karna O(n log n) per query — bekaar. Sorted array rakh ke insert karo to bhi O(n) per insert, kyunki elements shift karne padte hain.

Trick ye hai: median ko dhoondhna hi mat pado — use hamesha haath ke paas rakho.

Data ko do hisson mein baanto. Chhota aadha ek max-heap mein (taaki uska sabse bada upar rahe), aur bada aadha ek min-heap mein (taaki uska sabse chhota upar rahe). Dono heaps ka size barabar rakho, ya low ek zyada.

Ab median dono heaps ke top pe hi baitha hai — koi search nahi, O(1).

Insert karte waqt ek round-trip karo: naya number hamesha low mein daalo, phir low ka max nikaal ke high mein daal do, phir agar high bada ho gaya to uska min wapas low mein. Ye teen line hi dono invariants (sahi aadhe + balanced size) ek saath sambhal leti hain.
lessons.analogy:
Assembly mein bachon ko height ke hisaab se do lines mein baant do — chhoti line jisme sabse lamba bachcha aage khada hai, aur lambi line jisme sabse chhota aage.
Ab class ki "beech wali height" dhoondhne ke liye poori assembly nahi dekhni — bas dono line ke pehle bachche dekh lo.
Naya bachcha aaya to ek line mein daalo aur lines ko barabar kar lo — bas.
lessons.why:
Find Median from Data Stream ek classic hard question hai jo Amazon, Google aur Microsoft — teeno mein aata hai. Aur Sliding Window Median uska aur mushkil bhai hai.

Par isse bada faayda ye soch hai: jo cheez baar-baar chahiye, use dhoondho mat — usko apne data structure ke invariant mein rakho. Yahi soch LRU cache, sliding window maximum aur bahut saare design questions mein aati hai.

Aur ye batata hai ki tum streaming data ke saath soch sakte ho — real systems mein data aata rehta hai (stock prices, latency metrics, sensor readings) aur poora dobara sort karna namumkin hota hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Do heaps banao — low = max-heap (chhota aadha), high = min-heap (bada aadha).
2. Insert (teen line, hamesha yahi order):
  low.push(num)
  high.push(low.pop())
  if (high.size > low.size) low.push(high.pop())
3. Ye round-trip dono cheezein ek saath pakka karta hai — aadhe sahi hain, aur size balanced hai. Alag-alag if likhne ki zaroorat nahi.
4. Median: sizes barabar? → (low.top + high.top) / 2. Warna → low.top.
5. Faisla ek baar le lo ki low hi extra element rakhega, high nahi. Phir poore code mein wahi maano.
6. Sliding window median: window se nikalne wale element ko turant hataana mehnga hai — lazy deletion lagao aur size counters alag rakho.

qa.q: Why does this stay balanced?
qa.a: After every insert: add to low, move low's maximum to high, then if high is bigger move high's minimum back. That round-trip guarantees low always holds the smaller half and the halves differ by at most one — so the median is always at the two roots.

qa.q: What's the alternative to two heaps?
qa.a: A balanced BST (like a sorted array + binary search) also gives median, but array inserts are O(n). Two heaps make insert O(log n) and median O(1), which is why it's the accepted solution for streaming medians.

lessons.name: Heapify / Build Heap in O(n)
lessons.desc: Turning an arbitrary array into a valid heap. Sift down each node starting from the last internal node down to the root — this is O(n), not O(n log n). The intuition: most nodes are near the leaves, and their sift-down depth is small.
lessons.q: Why is heapify O(n) instead of O(n log n)?
lessons.qsub: What index is the last internal node of a heap? · Why is sift-down building faster than inserting n times? · How do you do heapsort with this? · Where does the O(n) come from mathematically?
lessons.what:
Ek random array hai aur usse heap banana hai. Seedha tareeka: har element ko push() karte jao. Har push O(log n), kul O(n log n).

Par ek behtar tareeka hai jo sirf O(n) leta hai — aur ye kaafi log ko surprise karta hai.

Heapify ulta chalta hai. Array ke aakhri internal node se shuru karo (i = n/2 - 1) aur root ki taraf peeche chalo, har node pe siftDown karte hue.

Ye sasta kyun hai? Kyunki kaam aur nodes ki ginti ulti taraf hain. Patte (poore ke aadhe!) pehle se hi valid heap hain — unka kaam zero. Unke upar wale n/4 nodes sirf ek level neeche jaate hain. Jo node poori height gir sakta hai wo ek hi hai — root.

Jodo sab — series 2n se kam pe ruk jaati hai. Isliye O(n).

Aur push wala tareeka mehnga isliye hai ki wahan ulta hota hai: aadhe nodes patton pe aate hain, aur siftUp mein unhi ko poori height chadhni pad sakti hai.
lessons.analogy:
Poori company ko seniority ke hisaab se settle karna hai.
Agar CEO se shuru karoge to har badlav poore neeche tak jaayega.
Par agar sabse chhoti teams se shuru karo — do-teen logon ko aapas mein sahi kar do — aur phir upar badhte jao, to upar tak pahunchte-pahunchte kaam bahut kam bacha hota hai, kyunki bade level pe log hi gine-chune hain.
lessons.why:
“Heap banane mein kitna time lagta hai?” — ye interview ka bahut aam sawaal hai, aur O(n log n) ek bahut aam galat jawab hai.

Sahi jawab dena, aur uske peeche ka reason ek line mein bol dena ("aadhe nodes patte hain, unka kaam zero hai") — ye turant dikhata hai ki tumne complexity ratti nahi, samjhi hai.

Practically bhi farq padta hai: Top-K jaise problems mein agar poora array pehle se hai, to heapify + k pops O(n + k log n) deta hai. Aur heapsort bhi isi pe khada hai — O(n log n) time, O(1) space, guaranteed (quicksort ki tarah worst case pe girta nahi).

Kaise sochein:

1. Aakhri internal node nikaalo: i = (n >> 1) - 1. Iske aage sab patte hain.
2. Loop ulta chalao — i se 0 tak.
3. Har node pe siftDown karo — siftUp nahi. Ye poora farq hai.
4. Ulta chalne ki wajah: jab tum kisi node pe pahunchte ho, uske dono children pehle se valid heap ban chuke hote hain. Isliye ek hi siftDown kaafi hai.
5. Sab kuch in place hota hai — koi nayi memory nahi, space O(1).
6. Heapsort: max-heap banao, phir n baar root ko aakhri element se swap karo aur size ek kam karke siftDown chala do.
7. Interview mein ek line bol do: "heapify O(n) hai kyunki aadhe nodes patte hain aur unka sift-down kaam zero hai."

qa.q: Why is heapify O(n) instead of O(n log n)?
qa.a: Because most nodes are near the leaves and sift down only a few levels. Summing each node's height over the whole tree gives a geometric series that converges to < 2n. Insert-based building is O(n log n) since n/2 nodes sift up the full height.

qa.q: Why start at the last internal node and sift down?
qa.a: A leaf is already a valid heap of size 1. Working bottom-up guarantees every child is heapified before its parent, so one sift down per node fixes the whole array. Sifting up instead would be O(n log n).

lessons.name: Timed Mock Sessions
lessons.desc: 45-minute, no-hints, talk-out-loud problem solving under a timer — the closest rehearsal for the real thing. You have been doing one per week since Phase 3 — here the cadence goes up to one every other day for 30 days (10+ more mocks). The goal is performance, not learning new algorithms.
lessons.q: How do you choose mock problems?
lessons.qsub: How do you handle a problem you've never seen? · When should you stop coding and talk? · How do you simulate the phone-screen format?
lessons.what:
200 problems solve ho chuke hain. Apne kamre mein, bina timer ke, editor mein chalate-chalate. Aur phir interview mein 45 minute milte hain, ek insaan tumhe dekh raha hai jab tum soch rahe ho, aur dimaag khaali ho jaata hai.

Ye knowledge ka gap nahi hai. Ye performance ka gap hai — aur ye alag se practice maangta hai.

Timed mock exactly wahi haalat banata hai: 45 minute ka timer, koi hint nahi, koi Google nahi, aur poore waqt apni soch zor se bolna — chahe kamre mein koi na ho.

Aur asli faayda mock mein nahi, uske baad ke review mein hai. Recording dekho — kahan 40 second chup rahe? kis point pe hint chahiye tha? complexity sahi boli thi? Har mock ke baad ek aadat theek karo.

Aaj naya pattern seekhna band. Ab jo aata hai, wo pressure mein nikalna seekho.
lessons.analogy:
Board exam se pehle full-length timed paper isliye nahi dete ki syllabus revise ho jaaye.
Wo isliye dete hain ki teen ghante mein time kaise baanto, aur ek mushkil sawaal pe atak jao to ghabrahat mein poora paper na chhoot jaaye.
Ye cheez chapter padhne se kabhi nahi aati — sirf ghadi lagakar baithne se aati hai.
lessons.why:
Interviewer sirf sahi answer nahi dekh raha. Wo char cheezein alag-alag score karta hai: problem solving (stuck hoke kya karte ho), coding (saaf code), communication (soch sunai de rahi hai?), aur testing (galti khud pakadte ho?).

Inme se teen ka LeetCode grind se koi lena-dena nahi hai. Wo sirf mock se aati hain.
