Aur ek practical baat: onsite mein 4-5 rounds back-to-back hote hain. Ye stamina ka bhi kaam hai. Agar tumne kabhi ek din mein do 45-minute session nahi kiye, to teesre round tak dimaag thak jaayega — aur wahi round decide karega.

Kaise sochein:

1. Ek naya problem chuno — dekha hua nahi. Apne kamzor pattern se.
2. Timer 45 minute pe lagao. Screen recording chalu karo (audio ke saath).
3. Poore waqt bolte raho. Chup baithna hi sabse badi galti hai — interviewer ko tumhari soch dikhni chahiye.
4. Brute force pehle bolo, chahe kitna bhi bewakoofi wala lage. Usi se optimization ka raasta banta hai.
5. Code shuru karne se pehle approach confirm karwao. Seedha likhna shuru kar diya to galat raste pe 20 minute ja sakte hain.
6. Aakhir mein khud test karo — ek normal case, ek edge case. Unke bolne ka intezaar mat karo.
7. Review (15-20 min): recording dekho, teen cheez likho — kahan chup, kahan hint chahiye tha, complexity sahi thi kya.
8. Har mock log karo. Ek hafte baad wahi problem dobara karo — ye retention batata hai, sirf pehli koshish nahi.
where: 15-20 min after · space: write down gaps

qa.q: How do you choose mock problems?
qa.a: Draw from your weakest patterns — the ones you mark 😰 in confidence scores. Rotate: one mock from a weak area, one from a strong area. Repeat the same problem a week later to measure retention, not just first-try success.

qa.q: What should the review focus on?
qa.a: Three things: (1) silence — where did you stop talking? (2) the moment you reached for hints — could you have pushed through? (3) correctness of your complexity analysis. Each mock should fix ONE concrete habit, not just 'do better'.

lessons.name: System Design Basics
lessons.desc: Design a large system in 45 minutes: requirements → estimations → data model → API → components → deep dive. For DSA interviews, a basic framework beats memorized systems — know URL shortener, rate limiter, and chat app cold.
lessons.q: What's the difference between a senior and mid design interview?
lessons.qsub: When do you choose a queue over synchronous calls? · What does 'eventually consistent' mean for a feed? · How do you estimate storage for 100M users?
lessons.what:
Interviewer bolta hai “design a URL shortener” aur tum seedha database schema likhne lag jaate ho. Paanch minute baad wo poochta hai “scale kitna hai?” — aur jawab nahi hai.

System design round mein sabse bada risk improvise karna hai. Har baar kuch zaroori cheez chhoot jaati hai, aur baar-baar alag cheez chhootti hai.

Iska ilaaj ek framework hai jo tum har sawaal pe wahi chalate ho, topic chahe koi bhi ho:

Requirements → Estimations → Data model → API → Components → Deep dive.

Ye tumhe smart nahi banata — ye tumhe bhoolne se bachata hai. Aur interviewer ko dikhta hai ki tum ek dhundhle sawaal ko tarike se tod rahe ho.

Aur ek baat: yahan koi ek sahi jawab hota hi nahi. Score jawab ka nahi milta — trade-off bolne ka milta hai. “Maine ye chuna, iska nuksaan ye hai, aur is case mein wo nuksaan theek hai.”
lessons.analogy:
Wedding planner naye event pe seedha decoration nahi sochta.
Pehle kitne log aur kitna budget (requirements), phir venue kitna bada (estimation), phir kaun kahan baithega (data model), tab jaake stage aur catering ke details (deep dive).
Order follow karne se koi bhi bada function bina chaos ke nikal jaata hai — aur order todne se chhota function bhi bigad jaata hai.
lessons.why:
Senior aur Staff rounds mein system design onsite ka 40-60% hota hai. Mid-level pe bhi ab ek round aata hai.

Aur DSA se ye poori tarah alag skill hai. Wahan ek sahi jawab hai; yahan koi nahi. Wahan tum solve karte ho; yahan tum baat-cheet chalate ho.

Mid aur senior ka farq bhi yahin dikhta hai: mid-level candidate ko prompt dena padta hai ("aur caching?", "failure hone pe?"), senior wo cheezein khud uthata hai aur trade-off ke saath bolta hai.

Aur ek practical baat: teen reference systems cold yaad rakh lo — URL shortener, rate limiter, chat app. Zyadatar sawaal inhi ke tukdon se bante hain (hashing, sharding, queue, fan-out, websocket, cache).

Kaise sochein:

1. Requirements (5 min). Functional aur non-functional dono. Aur scope kaato — "analytics main abhi bahar rakh raha hoon, baad mein time bacha to wapas aaunga."
2. Estimations (5 min). DAU × requests ÷ 86400 = QPS. Peak = 2-3×. Storage = size × count. Number zubaani bolo — yahi sabse zyada log chhod dete hain.
3. Data model (5 min). Kaunsi entities, kaunsa index, SQL ya NoSQL — aur kyun.
4. API (5 min). Do-teen endpoint kaafi hain. Kya andar jaata hai, kya bahar aata hai.
5. Components (10 min). Box aur arrow. Client → LB → service → cache → DB. Queue tab jab kaam async ho sakta ho.
6. Deep dive (15 min). Ek mushkil hissa chuno — hot key, ID generation, consistency, fan-out. Trivial hissa chunna sabse badi galti hai.
7. Har badi choice ke saath uska nuksaan bhi bolo. Ye ek aadat poora round badal deti hai.
where: Req → Est → Data → API → Comp → Dive · space: ~10 min each

qa.q: What's the difference between a senior and mid design interview?
qa.a: Seniors are expected to drive the conversation and handle trade-offs — consistency vs availability, caching strategy, failure modes — without being fed prompts. A clear framework + explicit trade-off reasoning is what separates the two.

qa.q: How deep should estimations go?
qa.a: One or two levels: daily active users × requests per user → QPS; storage per item × items → total. Exact numbers matter less than the reasoning chain and order-of-magnitude sanity (thousands vs billions).

lessons.name: Spaced Repetition & Review
lessons.desc: Revisit every problem you got wrong across phases 0-8 at increasing intervals: next day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks. Re-solve WITHOUT looking at old notes. This converts 'I've seen this' into 'I can solve this cold'.
lessons.q: Why spaced repetition and not mass review?
lessons.qsub: How do you decide a problem 'graduated'? · What do you do with a problem that keeps failing? · How many problems should be in the active review queue?
lessons.what:
Ek hard DP problem solve ki. Solution samajh bhi aaya, accha bhi laga. Teen hafte baad wahi problem saamne aayi — aur tum phir se atak gaye.

Ye normal hai. Dimaag jo cheez use nahi hoti use hatata rehta hai, aur wo bhoolne ka pattern predictable hai.

Spaced repetition usi predictability ka faayda uthata hai: har galat problem ko badhte gap pe dobara solve karo — agle din, phir 3 din baad, phir 1 hafte baad, phir 2 hafte baad. Har baar jo tum theek us waqt revise karte ho jab bhoolne wale the, memory zyada mazboot hoti hai.

Aur sabse zaroori niyam: apna purana note khol ke mat padho. Pehle zero se solve karo. Note baad mein kholo — compare karne ke liye, prompt ke liye nahi.

Kyunki padhna sirf pehchaanna hai (“haan haan, ye to pata hai”), aur solve karna yaad aana hai. Interview sirf doosri cheez maapta hai.
lessons.analogy:
Gym diary socho. Ek weight ek baar utha ke chhod do — do hafte mein strength wapas normal.
Par wahi weight badhte gap ke saath baar-baar uthao (kal, phir teen din baad, phir hafte baad) — aur wo strength permanently baith jaati hai.
Aur ek din nahi utha paaye? To gap wapas chhota kar lete ho. Bas.
lessons.why:
Ye interviewer seedha nahi poochta — par uska result saaf dikhta hai. Jab problem padhte hi tumhe lage “ye sliding window hai” bina soche, wo spaced repetition ka nateeja hai.

Interview ka pehla aur sabse zaroori kadam pattern pehchaanna hai. Agar 5 minute usi mein chale gaye, to 45 minute mein poora solution likhna mushkil ho jaata hai.

Aur ye time bhi bachata hai. 300 problems solve karne se behtar hai 150 problems jo tum sach mein kar sakte ho. Log 300 karke bhi interview mein blank ho jaate hain — kyunki recall par kaam kiya hi nahi.

Kaise sochein:

1. Har din jo problem galat hui, ya jisme hint chahiye tha, ya jo bahut mushkil lagi — usse ek tracker mein log karo, aaj ki date ke saath.
2. Agle din: dobara solve karo. Bina note dekhe. Pehle zero se koshish.
3. Saaf ho gaya (time ke andar, bina hint)? Interval badha do — 3 din.
4. Atak gaye? Interval wapas 1 din pe le aao. Koi sharm ki baat nahi — system exactly yahi karne ke liye bana hai.
5. Ladder: 1 din → 3 din → 1 hafta → 2 hafte → graduate.
6. Solve karne ke baad apna purana note kholo aur compare karo — kya approach wahi thi? koi behtar tareeka tha?
7. Queue 10 se zyada mat hone do. Bada ho gaya to naye problems rok do aur pehle backlog khatam karo.
8. Ek hi problem teen baar fail? Wo problem ki dikkat nahi — us pattern ki dikkat hai. Topic wapas padho, phir queue mein daalo.

qa.q: Why spaced repetition and not mass review?
qa.a: Forgetting curves are predictable — revisiting right before you'd forget strengthens the memory most efficiently. Spaced intervals beat re-solving everything in one weekend both for retention and for time budget.

qa.q: Why re-solve before reading your own notes?
qa.a: Reading your solution first tests recognition, not recall — you'll nod along without being able to reproduce it. Re-solving cold forces retrieval, which is what an interview measures. The note becomes the comparison, not the prompt.

lessons.name: Behavioral Prep (STAR)
lessons.desc: 5 polished STAR stories (Situation, Task, Action, Result): toughest challenge, team conflict, failure + lesson, mentoring/leading, and a data-driven decision. Numbers and ownership language turn a story into a signal.
lessons.q: What makes a STAR story strong vs generic?
lessons.qsub: How do you answer 'tell me about a failure' without sounding bad? · What's a good question to ask the interviewer? · How do you handle behavioral questions in a system-design round?
lessons.what:
Recruiter poochta hai: “ek baar bataiye jab aapka kisi teammate se disagreement hua ho.” Aur tum paanch minute tak ghoomte raho — na saaf situation, na saaf result. Recruiter ko sirf itna dikha ki tum apna kaam clearly explain nahi kar paate.

STAR ek dhaancha hai jo tumhare asli experience ko ek tight 2-3 minute ki kahani bana deta hai:

Situation — kahan, kab, kya haalat thi (20%)
Task — tumhari zimmedaari kya thi (10%)
Action — tumne kya kiya, aur kyun (60%)
Result — kya nikla, number ke saath (10%)

Idea naya kuch banane ka nahi hai. Idea ye hai ki jo tumne sach mein kiya, usse aise frame karo ki interviewer ko saaf dikhe tumne kya socha aur kya kiya.

Do cheezein poora farq daalti hain: “hum” ki jagah “maine”, aur result mein ek number.
lessons.analogy:
Ek achi shaadi wali speech socho: pehle context (kaise mile), phir kya mushkil thi, phir kya hua, aur end mein ek saaf toast.
Jo speech seedha result pe kood jaaye wo khaali lagti hai; jo sirf details mein ghoomti rahe bina point ke wo boring lagti hai.
STAR bas kahani ko us tight shakal mein rakhta hai.
lessons.why:
Behavioral round har onsite ka pehla 30 minute hota hai — aur wahi round pehla impression banata hai jo baaki din chalta hai.

Interviewer isse isliye leta hai kyunki coding skill alag cheez hai aur team mein kaam karna alag. Wo dekhna chahta hai ki tum conflict, failure aur ambiguity ko asal mein kaise handle karte ho — hypothetically nahi.

Aur ye wo round hai jiski log sabse kam taiyari karte hain. Isliye yahan thodi si mehnat ka return sabse zyada hai. Bina prepared stories ke acche engineers bhi vague ya defensive lagte hain jab dabaav wala sawaal aata hai.

Bade companies mein levelling bhi yahin se hilti hai — scope, ownership aur impact ki bhasha isi round mein sunai deti hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Apne career se paanch kahaniyan chuno — sabse mushkil kaam, team mein takraar, galti aur usse seekh, kisi ko sikhaya ya lead kiya, aur data dekh ke liya gaya faisla.
2. Har ek ko STAR mein likho. Action sabse lamba — wahin tumhare faisle dikhte hain.
3. Number daalo. "Fast ho gaya" nahi — "p95 800ms se 120ms". Number na ho to pehle-aur-baad ka farq batao.
4. "Maine" bolo. Team ka credit ek line mein alag se de do, par apna hissa saaf rakho.
5. Zubaani rehearse karo aur record karo. Man mein padhna kaafi nahi — bolne pe hi pata chalta hai ki kahan ghoom rahe ho.
6. 2-3 minute mein rakho. Lambi ho gayi to chhoti karo. Interviewer aur poochh lega agar aur chahiye.
7. "Why this company" teen line mein taiyar rakho — wo kya karte hain (specific), tumhe kyun accha lagta hai, aur tum kya laoge.
8. Do sawaal unke liye taiyar rakho. "Koi sawaal nahi" bura signal hai.
where: S → T → A → R · space: 60/20/10 ratio on A
out loud, 3+ times · space: record yourself

qa.q: What makes a STAR story strong vs generic?
qa.a: Specificity and ownership. Use real numbers, name the tools, and make the interviewer feel YOUR contribution — not 'we'. The Action step should be the longest and show your decision-making, and the Result should be measurable.

qa.q: How do you prepare for 'why this company'?
qa.a: Three sentences: what they do (specific, not a tagline), why that excites you (tie to your experience), and what you'd bring (one concrete skill). Memorable, rehearsed, and adaptable to the interviewer's team.

lessons.name: Practice Platforms
lessons.desc: Where to grind: neetcode.io for pattern-based roadmaps, LeetCode weekly contests for speed under pressure, and Pramp/interviewing.io for free peer mocks. Use each for its strength.
lessons.q: NeetCode vs LeetCode Top 150 vs Grind 75 — how to choose?
lessons.qsub: How many problems a day is sustainable? · When do you use company-tagged problem sets? · What role do editorial videos play (and when do they hurt)?
lessons.what:
Random LeetCode problems shuru kar diye — kabhi easy array, kabhi hard graph. Do mahine baad problem count to badha hua hai, par kuch pakka nahi lagta.

Dikkat platform ki nahi hai. Dikkat ye hai ki interview teen alag cheezein maangta hai, aur ek jagah se teeno nahi aati:

1. Pattern pehchaan — problem padhte hi lagna ki "ye sliding window hai". Ye neetcode.io se aati hai, kyunki wahan problems pattern ke hisaab se lage hote hain, topic ke hisaab se nahi.

2. Speed — ghadi chalte hue solve karna. Ye LeetCode contest se aati hai. Hafte mein ek, 90 minute, aur asli faayda contest ke baad ke review mein hai.

3. Kisi insaan ke saamne bolte hue code karna — ye sirf Pramp ya interviewing.io jaise peer mocks se aati hai. Test cases tumhe judge nahi karte; ek insaan karta hai.

Aur ek baat jo bahut time bachati hai: kaunsi list chuni, ye sabse kam maayne rakhta hai. NeetCode 150, Grind 75, Top Interview 150 — 80% same problems hain. Asli faisla ye hai ki ek chuno aur poora karo.
lessons.analogy:
Gym mein alag machine alag cheez banati hai — treadmill stamina, weights strength, aur ek sparring partner asli fight ka feel.
Sirf treadmill pe teen mahine bhaagne se punch nahi seekh jaate.
Aur har hafte naya gym badalne se kisi bhi machine pe progress nahi hoti.
lessons.why:
Zyadatar log yahin time barbaad karte hain — roadmap badalte rehte hain, easy problems se count badhate hain, aur solution videos dekh ke lagta hai ki seekh liya.

Teeno mein se koi bhi interview jaisa nahi hai.

Contests khaas taur pe log isliye chhod dete hain kyunki wo uncomfortable hote hain — aur wahi unki asli value hai. Contest mein tum naya problem ghadi ke saath dekhte ho, bilkul waise jaise interview mein hoga. Rank bekaar hai; jo problem fail hua uska review sab kuch hai.

Aur peer mocks: ek ajnabi ke saamne bol ke code karna pehli baar bahut ajeeb lagta hai. Chauthe-paanchve mock ke baad wo normal lagne lagta hai — aur asli interview mein wahi farq dikhata hai.

Kaise sochein:

1. Ek list chuno — NeetCode 150 acchi hai kyunki pattern ke hisaab se lagi hai. Aur usse order mein karo, kood-kood ke nahi.
2. Roz 2-3 problems. Isse zyada sustainable nahi hai, aur review ka time bhi chahiye.
3. Har problem pe pehle khud 20-30 minute do. Uske baad hi solution dekho.
4. Hafte mein ek contest. Poore 90 minute. Rank bhool jao — review karo ki kaunse problem chhoote aur kyun.
5. Hafte mein ek peer mock (Pramp muft hai). Interviewer banna bhi utna hi sikhata hai jitna candidate banna.
6. Contests kab shuru karo? Jab mediums bina timer ke aaraam se ho jaayein. Usse pehle contest sirf demotivate karega.
7. Company tags onsite se 2 hafte pehle. Usse pehle karne ka koi matlab nahi.
8. Editorial video solve karne ki jagah nahi, uske baad — aur wo bhi tab jab tum apna attempt likh chuke ho.

qa.q: NeetCode vs LeetCode Top 150 vs Grind 75 — how to choose?
qa.a: They overlap heavily. Pick ONE structured list (NeetCode 150 is well-organized by pattern) and work it in order. The list matters less than consistent pattern-to-problem mapping and spaced review. Contests add the pressure dimension.

qa.q: When should you start contests?
qa.a: When you can solve mediums untimed consistently — contests measure speed, and speed without correctness is noise. One contest a week is enough; the real value is the post-contest review of problems you failed.
